exercises.name: Back Squat
cues: Bar on the shelf of your shoulders, not your neck; squeeze the shoulder blades.
Big breath in and brace before you unrack, not after.
Sit down between your hips, knees tracking over your toes.
Drive the whole foot into the floor on the way up.

exercises.name: Front Squat
cues: Elbows high, bar resting on your shoulders -- the fingers only guide it.
When the elbows drop the bar follows, so keep them up all the way.
Stay upright and sit straight down between the hips.
Expect noticeably less than your back squat.

exercises.name: Box Squat
cues: Set the box so the hip crease lands just below the top of the knee.
Sit BACK onto it with the shins upright, then pause without rocking.
Stay tight on the box -- do not relax onto it and bounce back up.
The box sets the depth, so every rep in the set is the same depth.

exercises.name: Pause Squat
cues: Squat to your normal depth and hold there for a full two-count.
Stay braced through the pause; the bar must not drift forward.
Drive straight up out of the hole with no bounce -- that is the whole point.
It will feel far heavier than the same bar squatted at normal speed.

exercises.name: Safety Bar Squat
cues: The padded yoke sits on your shoulders; hold the handles in front of you.
It tips you forward more than a straight bar -- fight to stay upright.
Useful on days your shoulders will not let you hold a normal bar.

exercises.name: Overhead Squat
cues: Snatch grip, bar locked out and stacked over the middle of the foot.
Push up into the bar the whole way down; the arms never soften.
Go only as deep as you can hold the bar back -- ankles and shoulders decide.
Mobility fails here long before strength does. End the set when it drifts.

exercises.name: Zercher Squat
cues: Bar in the crook of the elbows, hands together, elbows in front of the ribs.
Sit straight down with the chest tall; the bar is trying to fold you over.
Brace hard -- this position gives out at the trunk before the legs do.
It bruises the elbows at first; a towel over the bar makes it tolerable.

exercises.name: Snatch-Grip Deadlift
cues: Grip the bar wide, at the rings, so the hips start lower.
Chest up and shoulders pulled back before the bar moves.
Expect a lot less weight than a normal deadlift -- that is the point.

exercises.name: Weighted Chin-Up
cues: Palms toward you, hands about shoulder width.
Start from a dead hang and pull the collarbones to the bar.
Lower under control -- do not drop out of the top.

exercises.name: Weighted Dip
cues: Lean the torso forward slightly and let the elbows travel back.
Stop when the upper arms reach parallel -- deeper is not better here.
Keep the shoulders down and away from the ears throughout.

exercises.name: Belt Squat
cues: The load hangs from the hips, so the spine carries nothing.
Stand tall and squat between the handles without pulling on them.
Useful on a day when the back is the part that is tired.

exercises.name: Goblet Squat
cues: Hold a bell against the chest with the elbows tucked under it.
Sit straight down between the hips with the chest staying up.
Let the elbows brush the inside of the knees at the bottom.
The bell is a counterweight -- it lets you sit deeper than a bar does.

exercises.name: Leg Press
cues: Feet about shoulder-width and level, in the middle of the platform.
Lower until the knees reach a right angle, or as far as the hips allow.
Push through the whole foot and stop just short of locking the knees.
Never let the lower back round off the pad. That is what sets the depth.

exercises.name: Hack Squat (Machine)
cues: Shoulders under the pads, feet a little forward of the hips.
Sit down slowly with the back flat against the pad the whole way.
Drive up through the heels without slamming the knees straight at the top.
The machine holds you upright, so the quads get nowhere to hide.

exercises.name: Deadlift
cues: Bar over mid-foot, shins almost touching it before you take your grip.
Chest up, lats tight, and pull the slack out of the bar before you pull.
Push the floor away rather than yanking the bar up.
Finish standing tall -- do not lean back at the top.

exercises.name: Trap Bar Deadlift
cues: Stand in the middle of the bar with the handles level at your sides.
More like a squat than a straight-bar pull -- the knees bend more.
Chest up, push the floor away, stand tall to finish.
Expect a little more than your straight-bar deadlift.

exercises.name: Sumo Deadlift
cues: Wide stance, toes turned out, hands gripping inside your knees.
Open the hips and push the knees out as you set up.
The bar stays against your legs the whole way up.
Hips and shoulders rise together -- do not let the hips shoot up first.

exercises.name: Romanian Deadlift
cues: Start standing, then push the hips back with only a soft bend in the knee.
The bar stays in contact with your thighs the whole way down.
Stop when the hamstrings run out, not when the bar reaches the floor.
Much lighter than a deadlift -- this is a hamstring lift, not a pull.

exercises.name: Deficit Deadlift
cues: Stand on a plate or a low block -- an inch or two, no more.
Same setup as a floor pull, with more knee bend and a longer way to travel.
Hold the back angle; the deficit exposes a rounding back faster than the floor.
Longer range, so the bar is lighter than what you pull from the floor.

exercises.name: Rack Pull (Above Knee)
cues: Set the pins so the bar starts just above your kneecaps.
Higher pins mean a shorter pull -- the load is not comparable to a floor deadlift.
Shoulders back and lats tight before you break it off the pins.
Lower it back to the pins under control; do not bounce it.

exercises.name: Good Morning
cues: Bar on the back as for a squat, feet hip-width, knees softly bent.
Push the hips straight back and let the chest fall towards parallel.
Stop where the lower back would round, not where the hamstrings complain.
Start lighter than feels necessary. This one is not worth being brave on.

exercises.name: Single-Leg Romanian Deadlift
cues: Bell in the hand opposite the standing leg.
Hinge over the standing leg and let the free leg travel back behind you.
Hips stay square to the floor -- do not let the free hip roll open.
Balance gives out before the hamstring does; touch a wall if you need to.

exercises.name: Barbell Hip Thrust
cues: Shoulder blades on the bench, feet flat, shins vertical at the top.
Pad the bar across your hips -- it will dig in otherwise.
Squeeze the glutes to finish and keep your ribs down.
Chin tucked: look forward, not up at the ceiling.

exercises.name: Glute-Ham Raise
cues: Knees just behind the pad, feet locked in, body in one line to the head.
Lower under control without folding at the hips.
Pull yourself back up with the hamstrings, keeping that same straight line.
Brutal the first time. Push off a wall or use a band until it is not.

exercises.name: Nordic Hamstring Curl
cues: Kneel with the ankles held down and the body straight from knee to head.
Lower as slowly as you can and catch yourself on the hands.
Push off the floor to get back up; the lowering is the whole exercise.
Famous for wrecking hamstrings for days. Two or three reps is a first go.

exercises.name: Kettlebell Swing
cues: Hike the bell back between the legs with the forearms against the thighs.
Snap the hips through -- the arms are ropes and do not lift anything.
The bell floats to chest height and no higher; it is a hinge, not a squat.
Finish every rep standing tall with the glutes locked.

exercises.name: Back Extension
cues: Pads at the hip crease so the hips can move freely over them.
Round down under control, then extend to a straight line and stop there.
Do not arch past straight at the top. The lower back gains nothing there.

exercises.name: Cable Pull-Through
cues: Face away from the low pulley with the rope passed between the legs.
Push the hips back until the hamstrings load and the chest falls forward.
Stand up by squeezing the glutes, never by pulling with the arms.

exercises.name: Power Clean
cues: Bar over mid-foot, shoulders just in front of it, chest up.
Be patient off the floor -- speed comes after the bar passes the knee.
Extend the hips hard, then whip the elbows through and catch in a quarter squat.
Technique before load: this punishes years off far more than a squat does.

exercises.name: Hang Power Clean
cues: Stand tall first, then hinge the bar down to just above the knee.
No pull from the floor -- the lift starts from that hang.
Extend hard, drop under, and catch it high with the elbows through fast.
A little lighter than your power clean.

exercises.name: High Hang Clean
cues: Start from mid-thigh, barely below the hip crease.
The shortest pull there is -- almost all of it is speed under the bar.
Elbows whip through and the catch is high and shallow.
Lighter again than the hang version; go by feel, not ego.

exercises.name: Squat Clean
cues: Pull as for a power clean, then keep dropping into a full front squat.
Meet the bar early -- do not wait and catch it low and slow.
Stand up out of the bottom before thinking about the next rep.

exercises.name: Clean Pull
cues: The same pull as a power clean, except you never catch the bar.
Stay over it, then finish tall on the toes with the shoulders shrugged.
Arms stay long -- the legs and hips do the work, not a shrug-and-yank.
Set it down under control rather than dropping it from the top.

exercises.name: Clean High Pull
cues: A clean pull that keeps going: the elbows rise high and stay outside.
Elbows lead and stay above the wrists all the way up.
The bar travels further than a clean pull, so it takes less weight.

exercises.name: Power Snatch
cues: Wide grip out at the rings, bar over mid-foot.
Patient off the floor, then extend violently once it passes the knee.
Punch straight under it and lock the arms hard overhead in a quarter squat.
The most technical lift in here -- start far lighter than you think.

exercises.name: Hang Power Snatch
cues: Wide grip, stand tall, then hinge the bar down to just above the knee.
No floor pull -- extend from the hang and punch straight under it.
Lock the arms hard overhead, then stand it up.
A little lighter than your power snatch.

exercises.name: Snatch Pull
cues: The power snatch pull without the catch, wide grip throughout.
Stay over the bar, then finish tall on the toes with a hard shrug.
Arms stay long -- this is not an upright row.
Control it back down; do not let it drag you forward.

exercises.name: Muscle Snatch
cues: Snatch grip, pull from the hip or the floor, and never re-bend the knees.
Pull the bar up the body and turn it over without dropping under it.
Punch it to lockout overhead with the feet flat and still.
Light and fast. This is a technique drill, not a lift to test.

exercises.name: Dumbbell Snatch
cues: One bell between the feet, hinge down and take it with a flat back.
Drive the hips and keep it close to the body, elbow leading high.
Punch the hand up and lock the arm out as you drop under it.
Same reps on each side, and change hands without resting between them.

exercises.name: Kettlebell Clean
cues: Hike the bell back between the legs exactly as you would to swing it.
Snap the hips and keep it close, steering it around the wrist.
Catch it in the rack with the forearm vertical and the bell resting.
If it thumps the wrist you are casting it out instead of steering it.

exercises.name: Walking Lunge
cues: Step out and drop the back knee towards the floor, not forwards.
Push through the front heel to bring the back foot through.
Stay tall; the torso does not fold over the front leg.
Long strides load the glutes, short strides load the quads.

exercises.name: Reverse Lunge
cues: Step BACK and lower the back knee towards the floor behind you.
The front foot never moves and the weight stays through its heel.
Push off the front leg to stand, without pulling with the back foot.
Kinder to the knees than a forward lunge, so it is the one to start on.

exercises.name: Forward Lunge
cues: Step forward and lower the back knee towards the floor behind you.
Land heel first and keep the front knee tracking over that foot.
Push back off the front leg to return; do not walk out of it.
Harder on the front knee than a reverse lunge, so start lighter.

exercises.name: Rear-Foot-Elevated Split Squat
cues: Back foot on the bench, front foot far enough out to sit straight down.
Drop the back knee towards the floor; the front shin stays near upright.
Keep the weight through the front heel -- the back leg only balances you.
If the front knee aches, step the front foot further out and go again.

exercises.name: Split Squat
cues: Set the feet in a lunge and leave them there for the whole set.
Drop straight down, back knee towards the floor, torso upright.
Push through the front heel; the back leg balances, it does not drive.

exercises.name: Front-Foot-Elevated Split Squat
cues: Front foot up on a plate, back foot on the floor in a lunge stance.
The raised foot lets you sink deeper, so expect more stretch down low.
Torso upright and the front heel stays glued to the plate throughout.
Go lighter than a flat split squat -- the depth is the point, not load.

exercises.name: Front-Rack Barbell Lunge
cues: Bar in a front rack, elbows high and ribs down before you step.
Step out far enough that the front shin is still upright at the bottom.
Push back through the front heel with the torso vertical the whole way.
Elbows dropping is the sign to stop -- the bar rolls off a soft rack.

exercises.name: Step-Up
cues: Box at about knee height, and the whole foot on top before you push.
Drive up through the top foot only -- no push off the trailing toe.
Lower yourself back down under control instead of dropping off.
If you have to hop up, the box is too tall or the bells are too heavy.

exercises.name: Lateral Step-Up
cues: Stand side-on to the box with the near foot flat on top of it.
Drive up through that foot alone; the far leg must not push off.
Stand tall at the top without letting the free-side hip drop.
Lower under control and touch the floor lightly, do not land on it.

exercises.name: Lateral Lunge
cues: Step wide to the side and sit back into that hip with a flat back.
The trailing leg stays straight with the whole foot flat on the floor.
Push off the bent leg to come back to the middle.
Groin and inner thigh are the point, so ease into the range early on.

exercises.name: Deficit Reverse Lunge
cues: Stand on a low box and step back off it into a reverse lunge.
The extra height means the back knee travels further down than usual.
Front shin stays upright with the weight through that heel.
More range than a floor lunge, so start lighter than you think you need.

exercises.name: Cossack Squat
cues: Feet wide, sit into one hip and keep that whole foot on the floor.
The other leg stays straight with the toes turned up off the ground.
Stay as tall as the hips allow, then push back to the middle.
Hold something light out in front as a counterweight if you tip backwards.

exercises.name: Bench Press
cues: Shoulder blades pulled together and down, feet planted on the floor.
Bar to the lower chest with the elbows around 45 degrees, not flared wide.
Push yourself away from the bar as much as you push the bar off you.
Use a spotter or set the rack pins for anything heavy.

exercises.name: Incline Bench Press
cues: Bench at about 30 degrees -- steeper turns it into a shoulder press.
Bar to the upper chest, just below the collarbone.
Shoulder blades stay pinned back even on the incline.

exercises.name: Close-Grip Bench Press
cues: Hands about shoulder-width -- close, not touching in the middle.
Elbows tuck in towards the ribs and the bar lands on the lower chest.
Keep the wrists stacked over the elbows rather than bent back.
The triceps run out before the chest does, so the last rep arrives early.

exercises.name: Floor Press
cues: Lie on the floor under the bar with the knees bent and the feet flat.
Lower until the upper arms rest on the floor, pause, then press.
The floor sets the depth -- do not bounce the elbows off it.
No leg drive and no arch, so it is all shoulder, triceps and chest.

exercises.name: Pause Bench Press
cues: Lower to the chest and hold it there, dead still, for a full one-count.
Stay tight through the pause: shoulder blades pinned, feet planted.
Press from a dead stop -- there is no stretch left to help you.
It takes the bounce away, which is exactly why it feels heavier.

exercises.name: Dumbbell Bench Press
cues: Start with the bells on the thighs and kick them up as you lie back.
Elbows at about 45 degrees from the ribs, not flared straight out.
Press up and slightly together without clashing them at the top.
The stretch at the bottom is the point; go lower than a bar would allow.

exercises.name: Incline Dumbbell Press
cues: Bench at about thirty degrees. Steeper turns it into a shoulder press.
Bells at the outside of the chest, elbows about 45 degrees from the ribs.
Press up and slightly together, then lower back into a real stretch.

exercises.name: Push-Up
cues: Hands under the shoulders, body in one line from the heels to the head.
Elbows back at about 45 degrees, not flared straight out to the sides.
Chest to the floor, then push the floor away and spread the shoulder blades.
Hips sagging is the sign the set is over, not the arms giving out.

exercises.name: Depth Push-Up
cues: Start with a hand on each of two low boxes and drop to the floor between them.
Catch the fall and drive back up onto the boxes in one motion.
Stay rigid -- the hips must not sag as you land.

exercises.name: Smith Machine Bench Throw
cues: Use the Smith rails so the bar leaves the hands safely at the top.
Light load, maximal intent -- throw it, do not press it.
Catch with soft elbows and reset before the next rep.

exercises.name: Dumbbell Push Press
cues: Short dip from the knees, then drive the bells straight overhead.
The dip is vertical -- the chest must not tip forward.
Lock the elbows before the feet settle.

exercises.name: Landmine Push Press
cues: Hold the bar end at the shoulder, dip, and drive it along the arc.
The path is forward and up, not straight up -- follow the bar.
Keep the ribs down; do not lean back to finish the rep.

exercises.name: Kettlebell Jerk
cues: From the rack, dip and drive, then dip a second time under the bells.
The arms do not press -- the legs send it and you drop beneath.
Stand up out of the catch with the bells stacked over the shoulders.

exercises.name: Plyometric Push-Up
cues: Set up as for a normal push-up: hands under the shoulders, body rigid.
Drop under control, then push hard enough that the hands leave the floor.
Land on soft elbows and go straight into the next rep.
End the set when the hands stop leaving the floor, not when you tire.

exercises.name: Dip
cues: Start locked out with the shoulders pulled down away from the ears.
Lower until the upper arms are about parallel, leaning slightly forward.
Press back to straight arms without bouncing out of the bottom.
Hard on the front of the shoulder. Shorten the range if it pinches.

exercises.name: Landmine Press
cues: Bar end at the shoulder, opposite foot forward, ribs down.
Press up and forward along the arc the bar already wants to travel.
Do not lean back to finish a rep. If you have to, take weight off.

exercises.name: Machine Chest Press
cues: Set the seat so the handles sit at about armpit height.
Press out without letting the shoulders roll forward off the pad.
Stop just short of locking the elbows and control the way back.

exercises.name: Cable Fly
cues: Slight forward lean with a soft bend held in the elbows.
Bring the hands together in an arc -- the elbow angle never changes.
Let the chest stretch at the back of the movement without forcing it.

exercises.name: Overhead Press
cues: Strict: no dip and no leg drive. Everything overhead is priced off this PR.
Squeeze the glutes and brace so the lower back does not arch.
Move your head back out of the way, then push it through as the bar passes.
Finish with the bar over mid-foot and the biceps by your ears.

exercises.name: Push Press
cues: A short dip and drive from the legs, then press it the rest of the way.
The dip is shallow and straight down -- do not let it become a squat.
Legs start the bar, arms finish it.
Heavier than a strict press because the legs get it moving.

exercises.name: Push Jerk
cues: Dip and drive as in a push press, then drop back under the bar.
Receive it in a quarter squat with the arms already locked out.
Stand it up only once the bar is stable overhead.

exercises.name: Split Jerk
cues: Dip and drive, then split the feet front and back as you punch under it.
Front shin vertical, back knee soft, both feet landing at the same time.
The arms lock before the feet land, not after.
Recover the front foot first, then bring the back foot in.

exercises.name: Z Press
cues: Sit on the floor with the legs straight out and the bar at the shoulders.
Brace hard -- there are no legs and no bench to hide behind here.
Press straight up and finish with the bar over the middle of the head.
Ribs stay down. Not being able to lean back is the whole point of it.

exercises.name: Seated Dumbbell Press
cues: Sit tall with the back supported and the bells at shoulder height.
Press up and slightly in until the arms lock out over the shoulders.
Lower to at least ear height every rep; do not cut the range short.
Ribs down against the pad -- arching turns it into an incline press.

exercises.name: Arnold Press
cues: Start with the bells at chin height and the palms facing you.
Turn the palms outwards as you press, locking out overhead.
Reverse the turn on the way down so it finishes where it started.

exercises.name: Single-Arm Dumbbell Press
cues: One bell at the shoulder, feet planted, ribs down.
Press straight up without leaning away towards the empty side.
Squeeze the free hand into a fist -- it helps hold the trunk still.
Same reps each side, and the weaker side is what sets the number.

exercises.name: Handstand Push-Up
cues: Kick up to a wall with the hands a little wider than the shoulders.
Lower until the head touches the floor, then press back to lockout.
Stay stacked: ribs down, hips over the shoulders, back not arched.
If the rep is not there, lower slowly and step down. Do not crumple.

exercises.name: Lateral Raise
cues: Bells at the sides with a slight bend held in the elbows.
Raise out to shoulder height and no further.
Lead with the elbows, and lower slowly instead of dropping them.

exercises.name: Rear Delt Fly
cues: Hinge to a flat back with the bells hanging under the shoulders.
Open the arms out wide with the elbows staying nearly straight.
Light weight. If it turns into a row, the rear delts are not doing it.

exercises.name: Bent-Over Barbell Row
cues: Hinge to roughly 45 degrees and hold that angle for the whole set.
Pull to the belly button rather than the chest, elbows kept in.
Lower it under control -- no dropping and rebounding off the bottom.
If your torso rises to move the bar, it is too heavy.

exercises.name: Pendlay Row
cues: Hinge to a flat back near parallel to the floor and hold it there.
The bar starts on the floor and returns to the floor every single rep.
Pull it to the lower ribs fast; the torso does not rise with the bar.
The moment the chest lifts to help, the set is finished.

exercises.name: Single-Arm Dumbbell Row
cues: Hand and knee on the bench, back flat and level like a table top.
Pull the bell to the hip with the elbow tracking close to the body.
Let the shoulder blade travel at the bottom instead of locking the arm.
Hips stay square. Do not roll the torso open to get another inch.

exercises.name: Meadows Row
cues: Stand side-on to the end of the bar, feet staggered, free hand on the knee.
Grip the sleeve itself and row it up towards your hip in an arc.
Let the shoulder blade stretch forward at the bottom of every rep.
The arc is the point; do not fight the bar into a straight line.

exercises.name: Chest-Supported Row
cues: Chest on an incline bench with the arms hanging straight down.
Row the bells to the ribs with the elbows close to the body.
The bench takes the lower back out, so nothing moves but the arms.

exercises.name: Seated Cable Row
cues: Sit tall with a soft bend in the knees and the chest up.
Pull the handle to the stomach and hold the squeeze for a beat.
Let the shoulder blades reach forward at the front, but keep the back flat.

exercises.name: Inverted Row
cues: Bar at hip height, body straight from the heels to the head.
Pull the chest to the bar with the elbows close to the ribs.
Walk the feet in to make it easier and out to make it harder.

exercises.name: Suspension Row
cues: Handles at hip height, body straight from the heels to the head.
Pull the handles to the ribs and let the shoulder blades pinch.
Walk the feet forward to make it harder, back to make it easier.

exercises.name: Suspension Row with Rotation
cues: Row on one arm and let the free arm reach across and open the chest.
Turn from the mid-back, not by throwing the hips over.
Come back square before the next rep. Match the sides.

exercises.name: Single-Arm Cable Row
cues: Stagger the feet and hold the handle in one hand, arm long.
Pull the elbow past the ribs, letting the shoulder blade travel with it.
Resist the pull turning your chest -- stay square to the stack.

exercises.name: Half-Kneeling High Cable Row
cues: Half-kneeling, cable set high, handle in the hand on the down-knee side.
Pull down and back to the ribs with the ribs stacked over the hips.
Squeeze the down-side glute so the low back does not arch.

exercises.name: Side-Standing Rotational Row
cues: Stand side-on to the stack, handle in the outside hand.
Turn the back hip through and row the elbow past the ribs together.
The legs start it and the arm finishes it, not the other way round.

exercises.name: Mixed-Grip Pull-Up
cues: One palm forward, one palm back, hands about shoulder width.
Pull evenly -- the supinated arm will try to take over.
Swap which hand is which every set so the load stays even.

exercises.name: Half-Kneeling Landmine Press
cues: Half-kneeling, down knee on the same side as the pressing arm.
Ribs down and glute squeezed before the bar moves at all.
Press up and forward; the kneeling stance is what stops you leaning back.

exercises.name: Weighted Push-Up
cues: Plate flat across the upper back, someone else placing it if you can.
Same push-up: one line from heels to head, elbows back at 45 degrees.
If the hips sag under the plate, take the plate off rather than finishing.

exercises.name: Alternating Dumbbell Bench Press
cues: Both bells at the chest, then press one while the other waits down.
The resting bell stays locked at the chest -- it does not drift.
Alternate every rep and count the pair as one.

exercises.name: Single-Arm Incline Dumbbell Press
cues: One bell only, free hand resting on the thigh or out for balance.
Keep both shoulder blades pinned to the bench as the bell goes up.
The bench will want to twist under you -- do not let it. Match the sides.

exercises.name: Yoga Push-Up
cues: Start hips-high in a downward dog with the arms long.
Dive the chest through low, then press up into a long-arm finish.
Come back the way you came instead of dropping the hips.

exercises.name: Lateral Push-Up Walk
cues: From the top of a push-up, walk both hands and feet sideways one step.
Do a push-up, then walk another step the same way.
The hips must not swing -- travel with the whole body in one line.

exercises.name: Single-Arm Kettlebell Swing
cues: Hike the bell back on one arm, free arm out for balance.
Snap the hips through; the working shoulder stays down and packed.
The bell will try to turn you -- keep the shoulders square all the way.

exercises.name: Dumbbell Romanian Deadlift
cues: Bells in front of the thighs, knees soft and then fixed there.
Push the hips back and let the bells slide down the legs.
Stop where the hamstrings run out, not where the back rounds.

exercises.name: Slideboard Leg Curl
cues: On your back, heels on the sliders, hips lifted into a bridge.
Pull the heels in to the backside without letting the hips drop.
Straightening the legs back out slowly is the hard half. Go there.

exercises.name: Single-Leg RDL with Reach
cues: Hinge over the standing leg and reach the bell past the toes.
Reaching further is what makes it harder, not a heavier bell.
Free leg and torso finish in one line, hips still square.

exercises.name: Step-Up with Knee Drive
cues: Step up and drive the trailing knee to hip height at the top.
Stand tall on the box for a beat before the knee comes down.
No push off the bottom toe -- the top leg does all of it.

exercises.name: Goblet Single-Leg Box Squat
cues: Bell held at the chest, standing on one leg in front of the box.
Sit back until you touch the box, free leg out in front as a counterweight.
The bell up front is what lets you sit back without falling.

exercises.name: T-Bar Row
cues: Straddle the bar, hinge to a flat back, and take the handle with long arms.
Pull the handle to the stomach with the elbows tracking close to the body.
Let the shoulder blades spread at the bottom, then draw them back together.
Keep the hips still. If you have to heave it up, take a plate off.

exercises.name: Seal Row
cues: Lie face down on a raised bench with the bar hanging beneath you.
Row it up to the bench and keep the chest down the entire time.
No swinging is possible here, which is exactly why it is on the list.

exercises.name: Face Pull
cues: Rope at about head height, hands turning outwards as you pull.
Pull to the forehead and finish with the knuckles beside the ears.
Light weight and high reps. This is shoulder maintenance, not a lift.

exercises.name: Cable External Rotation
cues: Elbow pinned to your side, bent to a right angle, handle across the body.
Turn the forearm out and away without letting the elbow leave the ribs.
Light and slow. This is cuff work, so nothing here should look heavy.

exercises.name: 90/90 External Rotation
cues: Upper arm out at shoulder height, elbow bent to a right angle.
Rotate the hand up and back, keeping the elbow exactly where it is.
Stop where it starts to arch the back; that is the end of the range.

exercises.name: Mini-Band External Rotation
cues: Band round both wrists, elbows tucked at the sides and bent.
Turn both forearms outward against the band and hold a beat.
Keep the shoulders down; do not let them creep towards the ears.

exercises.name: W Pulldown
cues: Band anchored high, arms up and out so the body makes a W shape.
Pull down and back, driving the elbows into the back pockets.
Squeeze at the bottom for a beat. Small range, done properly.

exercises.name: X Pulldown
cues: Two bands anchored high and crossed, one handle in each hand.
Pull down and apart into a wide X, arms staying long throughout.
Finish with the thumbs turned back and the shoulder blades down.

exercises.name: Front Wall Slide
cues: Facing the wall, forearms flat on it, elbows at shoulder height.
Slide the forearms up the wall and let the shoulder blades travel with them.
Ribs stay down -- do not arch the back to get the arms higher.

exercises.name: Wall Slide with Low Trap Raise
cues: Slide the forearms up the wall as normal, then lift them off at the top.
Hold that lift for a beat; the muscle doing it sits low between the blades.
A very small lift is the right one. Height here is not the point.

exercises.name: Standing Cable Lift
cues: Side-on to a low pulley, feet planted, handle down by the far hip.
Drive it up and across to above the opposite shoulder, turning the ribs.
A lift is a chop upside down: low to high, and the hips start it.

exercises.name: Half-Kneeling Cable Lift
cues: One knee down, pulley low, handle starting outside the down knee.
Lift up and across to above the far shoulder by turning the ribs.
Squeeze the down-side glute so the low back does not arch to help.

exercises.name: Tall-Kneeling Cable Chop
cues: Up tall on both knees, pulley high, glutes squeezed.
Pull the handle down and across by turning the chest, not rowing.
Both knees down means neither leg can feed you any extra range.

exercises.name: Tall-Kneeling Cable Lift
cues: Tall on both knees with the pulley set low beside you.
Drive the handle up and across to above the opposite shoulder.
Hips stay square and forward; only the ribs turn.

exercises.name: Cable Push-Pull
cues: Side-on between two pulleys, one handle in each hand at chest height.
Press one arm out as the other rows back, in one movement.
The trunk must not turn at all -- resisting that is the whole exercise.

exercises.name: Half-Kneeling Cable Push-Pull
cues: Half-kneeling between two pulleys, a handle in each hand.
Press one arm and row the other at the same time, staying square.
Kneeling removes the legs, so the trunk has to hold you still alone.

exercises.name: Tall-Kneeling Pallof Press
cues: Tall on both knees, side-on to the cable, hands at the chest.
Press straight out and refuse to let the cable turn you.
Glutes squeezed and ribs down the whole time you are out there.

exercises.name: Tall-Kneeling Pallof Hold
cues: Tall kneeling, side-on to the cable, arms already pressed out straight.
Stay there. The cable pulls you round and you do not go.
Breathe normally through it rather than bracing and holding your breath.

exercises.name: Band Pull-Apart
cues: Arms straight out in front at shoulder height, band across the palms.
Pull it apart to the chest, squeezing the shoulder blades together.
Ribs down and the elbows straight the whole way through.

exercises.name: Pull-Up
cues: Hands just outside the shoulders, palms forward, hanging with long arms.
Pull the elbows down to the ribs and bring the chest towards the bar.
Come all the way back to straight arms between reps.
No kick and no swing. If the reps run out, use a band or a partner lift.

exercises.name: Chin-Up
cues: Palms towards you, hands about shoulder-width, arms long at the bottom.
Drive the elbows down and in; the biceps take much more of this one.
Chin clears the bar without craning the neck to get it there.
Usually the easier of the two, so it is the one to add reps on first.

exercises.name: Weighted Pull-Up
cues: Hang the plate or belt so it will not swing into your legs.
Start from a dead hang with the shoulder blades set.
Chin clearly over the bar, then lower all the way under control.
Add weight only once the bodyweight version is easy for reps.

exercises.name: Neutral-Grip Pull-Up
cues: Palms facing each other on the parallel handles, arms long at the bottom.
Pull the elbows down to the ribs and the chest up towards the handles.
The kindest grip on the shoulder, so it is the pull-up to keep if one hurts.

exercises.name: Lat Pulldown
cues: Thighs pinned under the pad, hands a little outside the shoulders.
Pull the bar to the collarbone with the chest up and the elbows driving down.
Let it rise all the way back and the shoulder blades reach up between reps.

exercises.name: Single-Arm Lat Pulldown
cues: One handle on the high pulley, seated or half-kneeling, one arm only.
Pull the elbow down towards your hip and let the shoulder blade follow.
Let the arm travel all the way up at the top without leaning away.
Match the weaker side's reps on the strong side, not the other way round.

exercises.name: Straight-Arm Pulldown
cues: Stand back from a high pulley with the arms straight and the elbows soft.
Sweep the bar down to the thighs without bending the arms.
Lats only. If the elbows bend it has become a triceps exercise.

exercises.name: Farmer's Carry
cues: Pick the bells up like a deadlift, then stand tall and walk.
Shoulders back and down, ribs stacked over the hips, no leaning away.
Walk at a normal pace. Do not shuffle, and do not race the clock.
Grip usually quits first. Put them down before the back starts to bend.

exercises.name: Goblet Carry
cues: Bell held at the chest in both hands, elbows tucked in.
Walk tall with the ribs stacked down over the hips.
The weight in front pulls you forward -- do not let it round your back.

exercises.name: Bottoms-Up Carry
cues: Kettlebell upside down at the shoulder, handle squeezed hard.
Wrist straight and the elbow tucked; walk without letting it tip.
Much lighter than a normal carry. The grip and shoulder decide the load.

exercises.name: Get-Up to Elbow
cues: On your back, one arm locked out over the shoulder, same-side knee bent.
Punch that foot down and come up onto the opposite elbow.
Eyes on the bell the whole way up and the whole way back down.

exercises.name: Get-Up to Hand
cues: Take the get-up to the elbow, then press up onto the flat hand.
Bottom arm goes straight and the chest opens towards the ceiling.
The top arm stays locked and vertical for every inch of it.

exercises.name: Get-Up to Hip Lift
cues: From the hand position, drive the hips up into a high bridge.
Three points on the floor: one hand and both feet. Hold it a beat.
Come back down the same way, one step at a time, bell still locked.

exercises.name: Skater Squat
cues: Stand on one leg with the other bent back behind you, knee down low.
Sit down until that trailing knee nearly touches, chest reaching forward.
Put something soft under the knee until the depth is reliable.

exercises.name: Kettlebell Rack Squat
cues: One or two bells racked on the forearms, elbows tucked to the ribs.
Squat with the chest tall; the front load will try to fold you over.
Keep breathing against the racked bells rather than holding your breath.

exercises.name: Goblet Slideboard Lunge
cues: Bell at the chest, one foot on a slider behind you.
Slide that foot back into a lunge and pull it home with the front leg.
Control the slide out. Letting it run away is where knees get sore.

exercises.name: Hands-Elevated Push-Up
cues: Hands up on a bench or box, body still in one straight line.
The higher the hands, the easier it gets -- this is the way to regress.
Same rules: elbows back at 45 degrees, chest to the bar, hips level.

exercises.name: Feet-Elevated Push-Up
cues: Feet up on a box, hands under the shoulders, body in one line.
More weight goes through the arms, and more onto the front of the shoulder.
Stop the set when the hips start to pike up towards the ceiling.

exercises.name: Feet-Elevated Inverted Row
cues: Heels up on a box so the body is level with the floor or above it.
Pull the chest to the bar and keep the hips from sagging behind you.
This is the hardest version before you start adding weight.

exercises.name: Band-Assisted Chin-Up
cues: Band looped over the bar with one knee or foot in the bottom of it.
Palms towards you, and pull all the way to straight arms each rep.
The band helps most at the bottom, which is where you need it.

exercises.name: Single-Leg Bench Hip Lift
cues: Shoulders on a bench, one foot planted, the other knee held up.
Drive through that heel until the hips are level with the knee.
Both hips rise together; do not let the free side drop away.

exercises.name: Lateral Sled Drag
cues: Side-on to the sled with the strap or handles held at the hips.
Shuffle sideways in a half squat, dragging it with you.
Come back facing the other way so both sides get the same work.

exercises.name: Kettlebell Deadlift
cues: Bell between the feet, hips back, chest up, arms long.
Push the floor away and stand tall, squeezing the glutes at the top.
This is the hinge to learn on before a bar goes anywhere near you.

exercises.name: Half-Kneeling Single-Arm Press
cues: Half-kneeling, pressing arm on the same side as the down knee.
Squeeze that glute and tuck the ribs before the bell moves.
Press straight up past the ear without leaning away from the weight.

exercises.name: Single-Arm Push Press
cues: One bell at the shoulder, feet under the hips, ribs down.
Dip a few inches and drive through the legs to start the bell up.
Do not let the load bend you sideways. Match the reps on both arms.

exercises.name: Hinge-Position Row
cues: Balance on one leg in a single-leg deadlift position and hold it there.
Row the bell to the hip without letting the hips roll open.
Balance quits before the back does. Keep the reps low and honest.

exercises.name: Pro Agility Shuttle (5-10-5)
cues: Straddle the middle line, then sprint five yards to one side and touch.
Turn, run ten the other way and touch, then five back through the middle.
Get the hips low into each turn. Standing tall is what costs the time.

exercises.name: Lateral Pogo Hop
cues: The same stiff-ankle bounce, travelling side to side a few inches.
Legs stay long -- do not turn it into a lateral squat jump.
Land on the balls of both feet and go straight back the other way.

exercises.name: Hip Rotator PNF
cues: Sit with one shin across in front, hinged forward to a light stretch.
Press that shin down into the floor for five seconds, then let go.
Take up the new range and repeat. Three rounds each side.

exercises.name: Banded Lat Stretch
cues: Band anchored high, one hand in it, then step back and kneel down.
Let the band pull the arm long and sit the hips back away from it.
Turn the palm up and down to move where the stretch bites.

exercises.name: Hamstring Roll
cues: Sit with the roller under one thigh, hands behind you taking weight.
Roll from above the knee up to the sit bone, pausing where it bites.
Bend and straighten that knee on a sore spot rather than grinding over it.

exercises.name: Suitcase Carry
cues: One bell in one hand and nothing in the other.
Stand dead upright -- do not lean away from the weight to balance it.
Walk the same distance on each side.
The side WITHOUT the bell is doing the work. That is the whole point.

exercises.name: Front-Rack Carry
cues: Bells in the rack, elbows down, forearms vertical against the ribs.
Ribs down and the breathing steady; it will want to go shallow.
Walk tall, and stop when the elbows start to drop.

exercises.name: Overhead Carry
cues: Lock the bell out overhead with the arm beside the ear, not in front.
Ribs down and the shoulder pushed up into the bell the whole way.
Walk slowly and look straight ahead.
Stop the moment the arm drifts forward. That is the shoulder giving up.

exercises.name: Trap Bar Carry
cues: Deadlift the frame up, then walk it without letting it swing.
Stand tall between the handles, arms long, shoulders pulled back.
Short controlled steps -- a swinging bar drags you side to side.
Set it down under control. A dropped frame is how toes get broken.

exercises.name: Sandbag Bear Hug Carry
cues: Hug the bag high on the chest with the arms locked underneath it.
Stand tall and let it rest against you rather than holding it away.
Breathing is the limit here, not the arms. Keep the steps steady.

exercises.name: Curtsy Lunge
cues: Step one foot back and across behind the other, like a curtsy.
Keep the hips square to the front -- do not let them open up.
Drive back up through the front heel, not the back toe.

exercises.name: Single-Leg Box Squat
cues: Bench at about knee height, stand on one leg with the other reaching forward.
Hold the bell at your chest -- it counterweights you and keeps you upright.
Sit down to the bench under control, then stand up through the standing heel.
Do not let the standing knee fall inward; raise the bench if depth costs you that.

exercises.name: Zercher Carry
cues: Carry the bar in the crooks of the elbows with the hands clasped.
Ribs down and elbows up -- the bar is trying to fold you forward.
Short steps, hard brace, shallow breaths.

exercises.name: Landmine Rainbow
cues: Hold the bar end at chest height, both hands, arms nearly straight.
Sweep it hip to hip in an arc and let the trunk turn with it.
Move the bar with the trunk -- do not throw it with the arms.

exercises.name: Cable Woodchop
cues: Stand side-on to the pulley with the feet planted wide.
Turn from the hips and ribs; the arms only carry the handle across.
Let the back heel turn with you rather than grinding it into the floor.
Same number of reps facing each way.

exercises.name: Landmine Rotation
cues: Hold the bar end at arms length in front of the chest.
Swing it side to side by turning the trunk, not by steering with the arms.
Let the hips and feet turn with it. The knees must not twist underneath.

exercises.name: Russian Twist
cues: Sit with the heels down or hovering, chest tall and back straight.
Rotate the ball from hip to hip, turning the ribs, not just the arms.
Stop if the low back rounds; that is the end of the set.

exercises.name: Half-Kneeling Cable Chop
cues: One knee down, the other foot forward, hips square and tall.
Pull the handle across by turning the ribs, not by rowing with the arms.
Kneeling takes the legs out, so the trunk has nowhere to pass the work.

exercises.name: Box Jump
cues: Step down off the box, never jump down -- that is where knees get hurt.
Land softly in roughly the shape you took off in, hips back.
Pick a height you can land on standing tall, not one you have to tuck for.

exercises.name: Seated Box Jump
cues: Sit on the bench with the feet flat and the shins upright.
No rocking. Every rep starts from a dead stop with no wind-up.
Swing the arms and jump up, landing soft on the box in a quarter squat.
Step down, sit, reset. The pause between reps is the whole exercise.

exercises.name: Countermovement Jump
cues: Dip fast to about a quarter squat, then jump straight up.
Arms swing back on the dip and up hard on the jump.
Reset fully between reps -- these are for height, not conditioning.

exercises.name: Squat Jump
cues: Start from a held quarter squat, pause, then jump with no extra dip.
Removing the countermovement is the whole point of the drill.
Land soft and settle back into the held position before the next rep.

exercises.name: Standing Long Jump
cues: Swing the arms back, dip, and drive forward and up together.
Aim for distance but stick the landing rather than stumbling out of it.
Full recovery between attempts -- these are maximal efforts.

exercises.name: Repeat Broad Jump
cues: Jump, land, and go again with as little time on the ground as possible.
Do not let the shins collapse forward on each landing.
Quality goes before the legs do -- end the set when the distance drops.

exercises.name: Depth Jump
cues: Step off the box. Do not jump off it.
On landing, spend as little time on the ground as you can, then jump up.
Start from a low box; height is earned over weeks, not sessions.
The most demanding drill here -- skip it if knees or ankles are sore.

exercises.name: Drop and Stick
cues: Step off a low box -- do not jump off it.
Land on both feet in a quarter squat and freeze there.
The rep is judged on the landing: no wobble and no extra hop.
This is the landing the harder jumps already assume you can do.

exercises.name: Hurdle Hop
cues: Bounce over each hurdle with the feet together and the knees cycling up.
Stay stiff through the ankles and spend as little time down as you can.
End the set when the heels start touching the floor.

exercises.name: Tuck Jump
cues: Jump and pull the knees to the chest, not the chest to the knees.
Land soft on the balls of the feet and go straight into the next one.
Stop when the knees stop reaching the same height.

exercises.name: Split Jump
cues: Start in a lunge, jump up and switch the legs in the air.
Land in the same lunge depth you took off from.
The front knee tracks over the foot on every landing.

exercises.name: Alternate Bounding
cues: Long, exaggerated bounds from one foot to the other.
Drive the free knee up and through on every bound.
Aim for distance and hang time, not turnover speed.

exercises.name: Single-Leg Bound
cues: Take off and land on the same leg, then repeat.
Land with the foot under the hip, not reaching out in front.
Heavy demand on one ankle and knee, so keep the sets short.

exercises.name: Band-Assisted Vertical Jump
cues: Band anchored overhead and looped under the arms or hips.
Jump as hard as you would unassisted -- the band is not doing the work.
Ride the band down and land soft; it will try to drop you fast.

exercises.name: Loaded Vertical Jump
cues: A light dumbbell in each hand, arms hanging -- no arm swing to help.
Dip and jump; if the height collapses, the weight is too heavy.
Land through the whole foot and reset before the next rep.

exercises.name: Squat-Hold Vertical Jump
cues: Sit into a quarter squat and hold it still for a count of three.
Jump from there with no extra dip -- that pause is the whole point.
Without the bounce to help, expect less height than a normal jump.

exercises.name: Forward Pogo Hop
cues: Same stiff-ankle bounce, but travelling forward a little each hop.
Knees stay nearly straight -- do not turn it into a broad jump.
Cover ground by pushing back, not by reaching with the feet.

exercises.name: Single-Leg Forward Pogo Hop
cues: Stiff-ankle bounces on one leg, travelling slowly forward.
Keep the hip and knee quiet; the ankle does the springing.
Short sets -- one ankle is taking every contact here.

exercises.name: Single-Leg Lateral Hurdle Hop
cues: Hop sideways over each hurdle on one leg and stay on that leg.
Land with the foot under the hip and the knee tracking out, not in.
Stop the set the moment you need a second hop to steady up.

exercises.name: Step-Up Jump
cues: One foot on the box, and drive off it hard enough to leave the floor.
The bottom leg is along for the ride -- do not push off it.
Land back where you started, same foot up, and reset.

exercises.name: Split-Stance Med Ball Scoop Throw
cues: Feet staggered, ball low and outside the front thigh.
Extend the back hip through and scoop the ball up and back.
Throw the same number from each stance before you stop.

exercises.name: Lateral Med Ball Scoop Toss
cues: Stand side-on to the wall, ball held low in both hands.
Load the near hip, then scoop the ball sideways into the wall.
The legs throw it -- the arms only steer.

exercises.name: Split-Stance Med Ball Shotput
cues: Side-on in a split stance, ball cupped at the shoulder.
Turn the back hip through and punch the ball into the wall.
One arm throws, so match the reps on the other side.

exercises.name: Lateral Bound (Skater)
cues: Push sideways off one leg and land on the other.
Stick the landing -- no hop or stumble once the foot is down.
Cover distance across the floor, not height off it.

exercises.name: Pogo Hop
cues: Small fast hops on the balls of the feet with the knees nearly straight.
All the spring comes from the ankles; the legs stay stiff.
Minimum time on the floor. Height is not the point here.

exercises.name: Line Hop
cues: Hop back and forth over a line, both feet together, as fast as you can.
Stay on the balls of the feet with light, quick contacts.
Feet and ankles are the target, so end the set when the rhythm breaks.

exercises.name: Med Ball Slam
cues: Reach the ball overhead with the ribs down, not arched back.
Slam it straight down in front of the feet with the whole body.
The hips and trunk do it; the arms only steer the ball.
Catch the bounce or let it die, but never chase it with a rounded back.

exercises.name: Med Ball Chest Pass
cues: Feet planted, elbows in, push explosively from the chest.
Throw hard enough that the ball comes back off the wall fast.
Catch and reset rather than rushing straight into the next rep.

exercises.name: Single-Arm Med Ball Chest Pass
cues: Ball cupped in one hand at the shoulder, feet planted square.
Punch it into the wall, letting the chest turn a little with the arm.
Catch it two-handed and reset. Match the reps on each side.

exercises.name: Half-Kneeling Med Ball Side Toss
cues: Half-kneeling side-on to the wall, ball held low in both hands.
Turn the ribs and throw it sideways into the wall.
Kneeling takes the legs away, so the turn has to come from the trunk.

exercises.name: Sprinter-Start Med Ball Chest Pass
cues: Set up in a staggered sprint stance, ball held at the chest.
Drive the back leg through and throw the ball out as you come up.
Legs and arms fire together. Throw it far, not high.

exercises.name: Stepping Med Ball Overhead Throw
cues: Ball overhead, then take two walking steps into the throw.
Let the hips lead and the ball come over last, like a throw-in.
Check the space ahead of you before the first rep.

exercises.name: Plank Row
cues: Top of a push-up with a hand on each bell, feet wide for balance.
Row one bell to the hip while the hips stay completely level.
If the hips twist, the bells are too heavy or the feet too close.

exercises.name: Side Plank Row
cues: Side plank facing a low pulley, handle in the top hand.
Row the handle to the ribs without letting the hips drop or turn.
Hold the side plank first; add the row only when that is solid.

exercises.name: Body Saw
cues: Forearm plank with the feet on sliders, body in one line.
Push back off the elbows so the whole body slides a few inches.
Come back the same way. The hips must not sag as you go out.

exercises.name: Compass Plank
cues: Hold a forearm plank and walk the feet round to one side, then back.
Four points: ahead, right, back, left, returning to the middle each time.
The shoulders stay put over the elbows; only the feet travel.

exercises.name: Push-Up Position Hip Flexion
cues: Top of a push-up, hands under the shoulders, body in one line.
Draw one knee towards the chest slowly, then put it back.
No bouncing the hips up. Slow is what makes this worth doing.

exercises.name: Push-Up Position Shoulder Tap
cues: Top of a push-up with the feet a little wider than usual.
Lift one hand and tap the opposite shoulder, then swap.
Hips dead still. Widen the feet if they want to rock.

exercises.name: Stability Ball Rollout
cues: Kneel with the forearms on the ball and the back flat.
Roll the ball away until the arms are long, ribs tucked down.
Go only as far as the low back stays flat, then pull it back.

exercises.name: Stability Ball Plank Rotation
cues: Forearms on the ball in a plank, feet set wide behind you.
Turn the forearms round the ball a little way, then back.
Small circles. The body stays in one line while the arms travel.

exercises.name: Suspension Fallout
cues: Stand leaning forward with a handle in each hand, arms long.
Let the arms travel out overhead, keeping the body in one line.
Squeeze the glutes and stop before the low back gives way.

exercises.name: Long-Lever Dead Bug
cues: On your back, but reach the opposite arm and leg out long and low.
The longer the limbs, the harder the low back has to work to stay flat.
Back lifts off the floor and the rep is over. Shorten the reach.

exercises.name: Short-Lever Dead Bug
cues: Same set-up, but keep the moving knee bent and the arm tucked in.
Short limbs make it easier -- this is the version to start from.
Low back pressed flat the whole time, breathing out as you reach.

exercises.name: Med Ball Overhead Throw
cues: Ball behind the head, then throw with the whole body, not the arms.
Hips and trunk snap forward first and the arms follow.
Let it go high and far -- do not try to control the finish.

exercises.name: Med Ball Rotational Throw
cues: Stand side-on to the wall with the feet planted.
Turn the back hip through first; the arms are last to arrive.
Throw the same number of reps on each side.

exercises.name: Tall-Kneeling Med Ball Throw
cues: Kneel tall with the hips locked out -- no sitting back on the heels.
Throw with the trunk and arms only; the legs cannot help you here.
Keep the ribs down instead of arching the back for more range.

exercises.name: Med Ball Backward Scoop Throw
cues: Ball low between the legs, then extend hips, knees and ankles together.
Throw it back over your head and let go of it completely.
Check there is nothing behind you before you start.

exercises.name: Acceleration Sprint
cues: Start low and rise gradually -- no popping upright in the first steps.
Push the ground back behind you rather than reaching forward.
Full effort the whole way; walk back to recover between reps.

exercises.name: Build-Up Run
cues: Start at a jog and add speed smoothly across the whole distance.
Reach about 90% by the end, then float -- never strain.
Shoulders and jaw stay loose the entire way.

exercises.name: Flying Run
cues: Use a 20 m run-in to reach speed before the marked zone.
Hold the speed through the zone; do not accelerate inside it.
Tall posture, relaxed hands, quick ground contacts.

exercises.name: Hill Sprint
cues: Lean into the hill from the ankles, not from the waist.
Short, punchy steps -- drive the knees, do not over-stride.
Walk all the way down; the descent is the rest.

exercises.name: Sled Push
cues: Arms locked out, body in one line from heel to head.
Short powerful steps, fully extending the back leg each time.
Keep the hips low -- rising up kills the drive.

exercises.name: Band-Resisted Sprint
cues: Set the band so it slows you slightly, never so it stalls you.
Hold the forward lean the band creates and push back hard.
End the rep when your form breaks, not when the band stops you.

exercises.name: A-Skip
cues: Skip with a knee drive to hip height, opposite arm forward.
The foot strikes down and back, directly under the hip.
One small hop per leg -- rhythm matters more than height.

exercises.name: B-Skip
cues: An A-Skip, then extend the lower leg forward at the top.
Claw the foot back down under the hip, never landing in front.
Hips stay tall; the reach happens below the knee only.

exercises.name: High Knees
cues: Knees to hip height, torso tall, no leaning back.
Quick ground contacts -- think frequency, not height.
Arms drive from the shoulder, hands to chin and hip.

exercises.name: Straight-Leg Bound
cues: Legs stay nearly straight; the motion comes from the hips.
Pull the ground back with the whole leg, landing on the ball of the foot.
Stay tall -- no forward bend at the waist.

exercises.name: Wall Acceleration Drill
cues: Hands on the wall, body in one line at about 45 degrees.
Drive one knee up, then punch the foot down under the hip.
The support heel stays off the ground for the whole set.

exercises.name: Ankling
cues: Stay tall and cycle the foot under the hip, never out in front.
Tiny steps -- the heel barely leaves the ground.
Land on the ball of the foot and snap it straight back up.

exercises.name: A-March
cues: Drive one knee to hip height with the opposite arm forward.
No flight phase -- one foot stays on the ground throughout.
Punch the foot straight down under the hip, not ahead of it.

exercises.name: Carioca
cues: Travel sideways, swinging the trail leg in front then behind.
Let the hips rotate freely while the shoulders stay square.
Quick feet -- the rhythm matters more than the ground covered.

exercises.name: Backpedal
cues: Sit into a low hip position and reach back with each step.
Stay on the balls of the feet -- the heels never touch down.
Keep the chest over the knees so you do not fall backward.

exercises.name: Lateral Shuffle
cues: Half-squat stance, feet pushing apart and never crossing.
Drive the ground away with the trail leg on every step.
Keep the head level -- no bobbing up and down.

exercises.name: Low Shuffle
cues: Drop the hips until the thighs are near parallel, and stay down there.
Shuffle sideways without letting your height change at all.
The quads burning is the drill working, not a fault.

exercises.name: Shuffle with Arm Swing
cues: Shuffle sideways and swing both arms across the body in rhythm.
The feet keep the same push-apart action as a plain shuffle.
Stay square to the front -- only the arms cross over.

exercises.name: Crossover Run
cues: Run sideways, crossing the trail leg over in front of the lead leg.
Open the hip toward where you are going as the leg crosses.
Cover ground -- this is a run, not a shuffle.

exercises.name: Lateral Crossover Skip
cues: Skip sideways, driving the trail knee up and across the body.
One skip per crossover, with a clear hop in between.
Shoulders stay level while the hips turn underneath.

exercises.name: Lateral Cross-Behind Skip
cues: Skip sideways, stepping the trail leg behind instead of in front.
The hip opens backward while the chest keeps facing forward.
Go slow enough to feel the hip turn, not just the feet move.

exercises.name: Lateral Skip
cues: Skip sideways with the feet pushing apart and never crossing.
Drive the lead knee up on every skip.
Land on the ball of the foot and go straight back up.

exercises.name: Carioca Short-Long
cues: Carioca with a short step in front, then a long step behind.
The rhythm is uneven on purpose: short, long, short, long.
Let the hips turn further on the long step than the short one.

exercises.name: Open-Up Run to Stick
cues: Turn the hips a quarter turn and run three or four steps.
Sink the hips and stick the last step with no extra shuffle.
Hold the landing for a full count before you reset.

exercises.name: Forward Hurdle Walk
cues: Step over each hurdle leading with the knee, not the foot.
Stay tall -- do not lean back to clear the bar.
Pause a beat on each landing before the next step.

exercises.name: Backward Hurdle Walk
cues: Walk backward over the hurdles, reaching back with the heel.
Look ahead, not down -- feel for the floor with the foot.
Lift the knee high enough to clear without twisting the hips.

exercises.name: Mini-Band Lateral Walk
cues: Band above the knees, feet wide enough to keep it under tension.
Step sideways without letting either knee fall inward.
Small steps, chest tall, no swaying side to side.

exercises.name: Mini-Band Skater Walk
cues: Band at the ankles, hips low in a quarter-squat.
Step out and back on a diagonal, like pushing off a skate.
Keep the band tight the whole way -- the feet never meet.

exercises.name: Butt Kicks
cues: Heels to the backside with the thigh staying under the hip.
Quick cycles -- frequency beats how high the heel gets.
Stay tall; do not let the hips tip forward.

exercises.name: High Knee Switches
cues: From a split stance, switch the legs in the air and land the same way.
One switch per rep, front knee up to hip height.
Land soft and reset before the next switch.

exercises.name: Straight Leg Skip
cues: Skip with the knee locked, swinging the whole leg from the hip.
Pull the foot down and back into the floor; do not reach out.
Toes stay pulled up toward the shin throughout.

exercises.name: Straight Leg Walk
cues: Walk with straight legs, kicking each one up and pulling it down.
The pull down is the point -- claw the floor back under the hip.
Keep the toes pulled up and the stride unhurried.

exercises.name: Power Skip for Distance
cues: Skip for ground covered rather than height -- long and low.
Push back into the floor instead of up off it.
Land under the hips and roll straight into the next skip.

exercises.name: A-Skip with Overhead Reach
cues: Skip forward with both arms reached overhead and held there.
Arms up makes staying tall harder -- do not arch the low back.
Keep the knee drive and the rhythm exactly as they were.

exercises.name: Standing Knee Drive
cues: Stand tall on one leg and drive the other knee to hip height.
Pause a beat at the top, toe pulled up and heel under the knee.
Squeeze the standing glute so the hips stay level.

exercises.name: Half-Kneeling Start
cues: Start from half-kneeling, back knee down, front foot flat.
Drive the back knee through and run out of the position.
Stay low for the first few steps instead of standing straight up.

exercises.name: Lateral Half-Kneeling Start
cues: Half-kneeling side-on to the direction you are about to run.
Turn the hips and push off the down knee in one movement.
The turn costs you a step -- make the first one count.

exercises.name: Fast-Leg Drill
cues: March three steps, then snap one leg through at full speed.
The fast leg cycles heel to hip, knee up, foot down.
Use the same leg for the whole rep; switch on the next one.

exercises.name: Falling Start
cues: Stand tall and lean from the ankles until you must catch yourself.
Let gravity start the run -- do not step until you have to.
Keep the first few steps low, pushing back instead of reaching.

exercises.name: Three-Point Start
cues: Front foot two shoe-lengths back, opposite hand down on the line.
Hips a little above the shoulders, weight forward onto the hand.
Rip the down arm back as the front leg drives you out.

exercises.name: Power Skip
cues: Skip for height rather than distance -- drive the knee up and hold.
The opposite arm punches to eye level as the knee rises.
Land under the hips and go straight back up.

exercises.name: Easy Run
cues: Conversational: you should be able to talk in full sentences throughout.
If you cannot, you are running a tempo run by accident.
Land under your hips with a quiet, quick turnover.

exercises.name: Warm-Up Jog
cues: Slow enough to hold a conversation the whole way -- this is not the session.
Let the arms hang loose and shake the shoulders out as you go.
Finish warm and slightly out of breath, never tired.

exercises.name: Tempo Run
cues: Comfortably hard -- sustainable, but talking is down to short phrases.
Hold one steady effort instead of starting fast and fading.
Ease into the first minute; do not sprint the opening.

exercises.name: Running Intervals
cues: Hard efforts with real recovery between them, not one continuous run.
Run the first interval at a pace you could repeat on the last one.
Keep walking or jogging through the recovery -- standing still stiffens you.

exercises.name: Fartlek
cues: Run easy, then pick a landmark ahead and push to it, then ease off.
The hard pieces go by feel, not by a watch -- twenty seconds to two minutes.
Recover at a jog rather than a walk before the next push.
Finish feeling like you had one more push in you. If not, they were too long.

exercises.name: Shuttle Run
cues: Mark two lines and run between them, touching the line every time.
Start slowing early and turn on a bent knee, never a locked leg.
Push hard out of the turn -- the change of direction is the training.
Turns punish stiff knees and ankles, so stop when they get sloppy.

exercises.name: Stair Run
cues: Run up on the balls of the feet with short, quick steps.
Drive the knees and use the arms; stay tall instead of folding forward.
Walk back down every single time. Running down is where stairs hurt people.
One step at a time to start. Two at a time is a different exercise.

exercises.name: Incline Walk
cues: A steady hill, or a treadmill raised enough that it stops being flat.
Stay upright and off the handrails -- hanging on removes the exercise.
Breathing hard but still able to talk. That is the whole prescription.

exercises.name: Air Bike
cues: Set the seat so the knee stays slightly bent at the bottom of the stroke.
Push and pull with the arms as well as the legs from the first second.
The resistance is made by your own effort, so the pace is entirely yours.
It is harder than it looks. Go slower than you think on the first interval.

exercises.name: Rowing Erg
cues: Feet strapped, shins upright at the catch, arms long and shoulders loose.
Legs first, then the back opens, then the arms -- in that order.
Come back arms, then back, then knees. Never pull with a rounded back.
Watch the pace, not the stroke rate. Long strong strokes beat fast ones.

exercises.name: Jump Rope
cues: The rope is the right length when the handles reach your armpits.
Turn it with the wrists, and hop just high enough to clear it.
Land on the balls of the feet with the knees soft on every contact.
The calves and ankles take all of this, so build the time up slowly.

exercises.name: Sled Drag
cues: Load it so you can keep walking. A sled you have to fight is too heavy.
Lean into the strap and drive through the legs with short steady steps.
Keep the arms relaxed -- the legs and hips move the sled, not the grip.
If there is room to drag it backwards, that is kinder on the knees.

exercises.name: Ruck March
cues: Pack the load high and tight against the upper back, straps snug.
Walk tall with a quick, short stride; do not lean forward from the waist.
Build distance before load; a ruck punishes the feet long before the legs.

exercises.name: Sled March
cues: Load it so you can walk continuously, not so you have to fight it.
Stay tall behind the sled, arms long, and drive through the legs.
Steady pace for time; if it turns into a grind, take weight off.

exercises.name: Backward Walk
cues: Walk backward over flat, clear ground, reaching back with the toe first.
Roll from toe to heel and keep the knee soft as the foot lands.
Glance over a shoulder now and then; never do this on uneven ground.

exercises.name: Trail Run
cues: Shorten the stride and pick the feet up more than you would on road.
Look three or four steps ahead, not down at your feet.
Keep the effort easy; let the terrain, not the pace, provide the work.

exercises.name: Front Plank
cues: Elbows under the shoulders, feet hip width, body in one line.
Squeeze the glutes and tuck the ribs down so the hips do not sag.
Brace hard and keep breathing; do not hold your breath.

exercises.name: Side Plank
cues: Elbow under the shoulder, feet stacked or staggered.
Push the hip up until shoulder, hip and ankle make one line.
Keep the top shoulder back; do not let the chest roll toward the floor.

exercises.name: Copenhagen Plank
cues: Side plank with the top leg's inner thigh resting on a bench.
Lift the hips and the bottom leg until the body is one line.
Start with the bottom knee bent; straighten it only when that is easy.

exercises.name: Hollow Body Hold
cues: Lie on your back and press the low back flat into the floor.
Lift the shoulders and legs just clear, arms reaching overhead.
If the low back lifts, raise the legs higher until it flattens again.

exercises.name: Dead Bug
cues: On your back, arms up and knees over the hips, low back flat.
Lower one arm and the opposite leg, keeping the back flat.
Move slowly and exhale as you reach; return, then alternate.

exercises.name: Bird Dog
cues: On all fours, hands under the shoulders and knees under the hips.
Reach one arm and the opposite leg out long, level with the back.
Keep the hips square; a glass of water on the low back should not spill.

exercises.name: Pallof Press
cues: Stand side-on to the cable or band with both hands at the chest.
Press straight out and resist the pull trying to rotate you.
Stand tall and square; the work is in not turning.

exercises.name: Ab Wheel Rollout
cues: Kneel with the wheel under the shoulders and the back flat.
Roll out only as far as the low back stays flat, then pull back.
Keep the ribs tucked; an arching back means you went too far.

exercises.name: Hanging Leg Raise
cues: Hang from the bar with the shoulders pulled down, not slack.
Raise the legs by curling the pelvis up, not just the hips.
Lower under control; no swinging between reps.

exercises.name: Toes to Bar
cues: Hang tall, shoulders active, and start from a small hollow.
Curl the pelvis and drive the toes up to touch the bar.
Control the way down; kip for rhythm, never for the whole rep.

exercises.name: Reverse Crunch
cues: Lie on your back, knees bent, hands flat beside the hips.
Curl the pelvis up so the hips leave the floor.
It is a short move; lifting the knees alone does nothing.

exercises.name: Cable Crunch
cues: Kneel facing the stack, hands holding the rope beside the head.
Crunch by rounding the spine toward the knees with the hips still.
The hips must not hinge; if they do, lighten the load.

exercises.name: L-Sit
cues: Hands on the floor or parallettes, shoulders pressed down.
Lift the hips clear and hold the legs straight out in front.
Tucked knees are the scaled version; keep the chest tall either way.

exercises.name: Bear Crawl
cues: On hands and toes with the knees hovering just off the floor.
Move the opposite hand and foot together, in small steps.
Keep the hips low and level; do not let them sway side to side.

exercises.name: Suitcase Hold
cues: Hold one heavy weight at your side with the shoulders level.
Stand tall and resist the lean toward the loaded side.
Grip hard and keep the ribs down for the whole hold.

exercises.name: Bicycle Crunch
cues: On your back, low back flat, hands resting light behind the head.
Bring one elbow toward the opposite knee by turning the ribs.
Do not pull on the neck; slow rotation beats fast pedalling.

exercises.name: Supine Windshield Wiper
cues: Lie on your back, arms out wide, knees bent over the hips.
Lower the knees toward one side while both shoulders stay down.
Go only as far as the shoulders stay flat, then return through the middle.

exercises.name: Side Plank Reach-Through
cues: Set a side plank, elbow under the shoulder, top arm to the ceiling.
Reach the top hand under the body, turning the ribs, then open back up.
Keep the hips high throughout; the rotation comes from the trunk.

exercises.name: Long-Lever Plank
cues: Walk the elbows out in front of the shoulders, body still in one line.
Squeeze the glutes and tuck the ribs down so the hips do not sag.
Brace hard and keep breathing; do not hold your breath.

exercises.name: Weighted Plank
cues: Elbows under the shoulders, with a plate laid flat across the upper back.
Squeeze the glutes and tuck the ribs down so the hips do not sag.
Brace hard and keep breathing; do not hold your breath.

exercises.name: High Side Plank
cues: Hand under the shoulder with the arm straight, feet stacked or staggered.
Push the hip up until shoulder, hip and ankle make one line.
Keep the top shoulder back; do not let the chest roll toward the floor.

exercises.name: Short-Lever Copenhagen Plank
cues: Side plank with the top knee, not the ankle, resting on the bench.
Lift the hips and the bottom leg until the body is one line.
Start with the bottom knee bent; straighten it only when that is easy.

exercises.name: Tuck Hollow Hold
cues: Lie on your back and press the low back flat into the floor.
Lift the shoulders clear with the knees tucked over the hips.
If the low back lifts, pull the knees in closer until it flattens again.

exercises.name: Dead Bug Heel Tap
cues: On your back, arms up and knees over the hips, low back flat.
Keep the arms still and lower one heel to tap the floor, back flat.
Move slowly and exhale as you lower; return, then alternate.

exercises.name: Bird Dog Elbow to Knee
cues: On all fours, hands under the shoulders and knees under the hips.
Reach the arm and opposite leg long, then draw elbow and knee together.
Keep the hips square; a glass of water on the low back should not spill.

exercises.name: Band Pallof Press
cues: Stand side-on to a band anchored at chest height, both hands at the chest.
Press straight out and resist the pull trying to rotate you.
Stand tall and square; the work is in not turning.

exercises.name: Half-Kneeling Pallof Press
cues: Kneel side-on to the cable, inside knee up, both hands at the chest.
Press straight out and resist the pull trying to rotate you.
Stay tall through the hips; the work is in not turning.

exercises.name: Barbell Rollout
cues: Kneel with a loaded barbell under the shoulders and the back flat.
Roll out only as far as the low back stays flat, then pull back.
Keep the ribs tucked; an arching back means you went too far.

exercises.name: Hanging Knee Raise
cues: Hang from the bar with the shoulders pulled down, not slack.
Raise the knees by curling the pelvis up, not just the hips.
Lower under control; no swinging between reps.

exercises.name: Decline Reverse Crunch
cues: Lie on a decline bench, knees bent, hands gripping behind the head.
Curl the pelvis up so the hips leave the bench.
It is a short move; lifting the knees alone does nothing.

exercises.name: Machine Crunch
cues: Sit in the machine with the pads on the chest and the hips set.
Crunch by rounding the spine toward the knees with the hips still.
The hips must not hinge; if they do, lighten the load.

exercises.name: Lateral Bear Crawl
cues: On hands and toes with the knees hovering just off the floor.
Step hand and foot out to one side together, then follow with the other.
Keep the hips low and level; do not let them sway side to side.

exercises.name: Straight-Leg Windshield Wiper
cues: Lie on your back, arms out wide, legs straight up over the hips.
Lower the legs toward one side while both shoulders stay down.
Go only as far as the shoulders stay flat, then return through the middle.

exercises.name: Barbell Curl
cues: Shoulder-width grip with the elbows pinned at the sides.
Curl without letting the elbows drift forward or the body lean back.
Lower under control all the way to straight arms.

exercises.name: Dumbbell Curl
cues: Bells at the sides with the palms turning up as you curl.
Elbows stay by the ribs; only the forearms move.
Same reps both sides, whether you alternate or finish one arm first.

exercises.name: Hammer Curl
cues: Palms facing each other and staying that way for the whole rep.
Curl to the shoulder with the elbows pinned to the sides.
Hits the forearm and the outer arm harder than a normal curl does.

exercises.name: Incline Dumbbell Curl
cues: Lie back on an incline bench and let the arms hang down behind you.
Curl from that stretched position without letting the elbows come forward.
The stretch at the bottom is the entire reason to do it on an incline.

exercises.name: Preacher Curl
cues: Armpits into the top of the pad with the arms flat along it.
Curl up, then lower all the way until the arms are straight again.
Do not bounce out of the bottom -- the elbow is exposed in that position.

exercises.name: Tricep Pushdown
cues: Elbows pinned at the sides and staying there for the whole set.
Push down to straight arms and squeeze at the bottom.
Only the forearms move. Leaning into it makes it a chest exercise.

exercises.name: Skullcrusher
cues: Bar over the shoulders with the elbows pointing at the ceiling.
Lower to the forehead or just behind it, keeping the upper arms still.
Extend back up without letting the elbows drift towards the hips.
Rough on the elbows. Use an EZ bar, and stop the set if it pinches.

exercises.name: Overhead Tricep Extension
cues: One bell in both hands pressed overhead, elbows beside the ears.
Lower it behind the head until the forearms pass the elbows, then extend.
Elbows keep pointing forward. They will want to flare out as it gets hard.

exercises.name: Barbell Shrug
cues: Bar at arms length with the shoulders relaxed all the way down to start.
Shrug straight up towards the ears and hold it for a beat.
No rolling the shoulders backwards. Straight up and straight back down.

exercises.name: Standing Calf Raise
cues: Balls of the feet on the step with the heels hanging free.
Drop the heels below the step, pause there, then push up to full height.
Slow on the way down. The stretch at the bottom is doing the work.

exercises.name: Seated Calf Raise
cues: Knees bent under the pad, balls of the feet on the platform.
Let the heels sink all the way down before pressing back up.
Bent knees move the work to the soleus, which wants higher reps than usual.

exercises.name: Tibialis Raise
cues: Back against a wall, heels on the floor a step out in front of you.
Pull the toes up towards the shins as far as they go, then lower slowly.
It burns fast. This is the muscle that gives out on hills and stairs.

exercises.name: Leg Extension
cues: Set the pad on the shins just above the ankles.
Straighten the legs fully and hold for a beat at the top.
Lower under control -- do not let the stack drop back onto itself.

exercises.name: Lying Leg Curl
cues: Pad just above the heels with the hips flat on the bench.
Curl the heels towards the backside and squeeze at the top.
Lower slowly and stop just short of the weight touching down.

exercises.name: Seated Leg Curl
cues: Sit back into the pad with your knees just off the edge of the seat.
Strap the lap pad down firmly so the hips cannot lift as you curl.
Curl the heels under the seat and pause before letting them back out.
