This stretches the hamstrings more than lying does, so start light.

exercises.name: Wrist Curl
cues: Forearms on a bench or the thighs with the wrists hanging over the end.
Let the bells roll down to the fingertips, then curl them back up.
Small range, high reps, slow. Speed does nothing at all here.

exercises.name: 90/90 Hip Switch
cues: Sit with both knees bent 90 degrees, front shin and back shin on the floor.
Rotate the knees over to the other side, keeping the chest tall.
Move under control; the hips do the work, not a swing of the torso.

exercises.name: Couch Stretch
cues: Back foot up the wall, front foot flat and forward of the knee.
Square the hips and tuck the tailbone under before leaning up.
Breathe out and hold; never force it past a strong stretch.

exercises.name: World's Greatest Stretch
cues: Step into a deep lunge, back leg long, front foot flat.
Drop the same-side elbow toward the instep, then rotate that arm to the ceiling.
Follow the hand with the eyes; one slow rep per side, never a bounce.

exercises.name: Kneeling Hip Flexor Stretch
cues: Half-kneeling, front foot flat, back knee under the hip.
Tuck the tailbone under first, then shift forward an inch.
The stretch belongs at the front of the back hip, not the low back.

exercises.name: Thoracic Extension over Foam Roller
cues: Roller across the mid-back, hands behind the head, hips down.
Extend over it a few inches at a time, pausing where it is stiff.
Keep the ribs from flaring, and never roll the lower back.

exercises.name: Quad Roll
cues: Face down with the roller under one thigh, weight on the forearms.
Roll slowly from above the knee to the hip, pausing where it bites.
Bend and straighten that knee on the sore spot instead of grinding past it.

exercises.name: Calf Roll
cues: Sit with the ball under one calf and that ankle crossed over by the other.
Work from the achilles up to the back of the knee, a little at a time.
Point and flex the foot where it is tender rather than rolling on.

exercises.name: Lateral Hip Roll
cues: Lie on your side with the ball just below the point of the hip bone.
Stay off the bone itself -- you want the muscle behind and below it.
Small movements, and breathe out on the tender spots.

exercises.name: Rotator Cuff Roll
cues: Ball between the wall and the back of the shoulder blade.
Lean in and roll small circles over the meat behind the shoulder.
Let the arm hang and swing gently while the ball stays put.

exercises.name: Pec Roll
cues: Ball on the wall, just inside the front of the shoulder.
Lean your weight in and search below the collarbone, not on it.
Raise and lower that arm slowly while the ball holds the spot.

exercises.name: Hip Rotator Roll
cues: Sit on the ball with that ankle crossed over the opposite knee.
Hunt around the back pocket area, not the tailbone.
Sit into it and breathe rather than rolling quickly over the spot.

exercises.name: Lat Roll
cues: On your side, roller under the armpit, that arm stretched overhead.
Roll the few inches down the side of the ribs and back again.
Turn slightly forward and back to find the edge of the muscle.

exercises.name: Upper Back Roll
cues: Roller across the upper back, hands behind the head, hips up.
Roll between the shoulder blades and the base of the neck only.
Stop where the ribs end -- the lower back is not rolled here.

exercises.name: Adductor Roll
cues: Face down with one knee out to the side, roller along the inner thigh.
Work from above the knee up towards the groin, stopping short of it.
Rock a few inches at a time; this one is tender, so go slowly.

exercises.name: Glute Roll
cues: Sit on the roller, one ankle crossed onto the opposite knee.
Lean into the crossed side and roll the whole back pocket.
Keep the hands behind you carrying some weight if it is too sharp.

exercises.name: Hip Flexor Roll
cues: Face down with the ball just inside the front of the hip bone.
Rest your weight on it and bend that knee slowly to floss the tissue.
Come off it if you feel a pulse under the ball; that is not muscle.

exercises.name: Half-Kneeling Ankle PNF
cues: Half-kneeling, front foot flat, and drive the knee out over the toes.
At the end of the range press the toes down hard for five seconds.
Relax and you will find a little more range. Repeat three times.

exercises.name: Three-Way Ankle Mobilization
cues: Front foot flat, then drive the knee straight over the toes.
Repeat driving it over the inside edge, then over the outside edge.
The heel stays down for all three. That is the whole rule.

exercises.name: Straight-Knee Ankle Mobilization
cues: Back leg long with the knee locked and the heel pressed down.
Lean into the wall until the calf pulls high up behind the knee.
A locked knee is what moves this off the soleus and onto the calf.

exercises.name: Standing Ankle Mobilization
cues: Stand with one foot ahead and rock that knee forward over the toes.
Keep the heel glued down; the moment it lifts you have gone too far.
Rock in and out rather than holding at the end.

exercises.name: Anterior Ankle Stretch
cues: Kneel with the top of one foot flat on the floor behind you.
Sit back until the front of that ankle and shin stretch.
Ease off if it pinches inside the joint rather than pulling in front.

exercises.name: Toe Sitting
cues: Kneel with the toes tucked under and sit back onto the heels.
Take weight through the hands at first -- this one is sharp underfoot.
Build up the time you can sit here rather than forcing it today.

exercises.name: Straight-Knee Calf PNF
cues: Back leg straight against the wall, heel down, calf on stretch.
Push the ball of the foot into the floor hard for five seconds.
Let go, take up the new slack, and go again three times.

exercises.name: Seated 90/90 Hip PNF
cues: Sit with the front shin and back shin both at right angles.
Press the front shin down into the floor for five seconds, then relax.
Lean a little further over the front leg each time you let go.

exercises.name: Seated 90/90 with Reach Across
cues: Sit in the 90/90 shape and reach the far arm across past the front knee.
Let the chest turn with the reach instead of only the arm going.
Keep both sit bones down as you rotate over the front hip.

exercises.name: Seated 90/90 Hip External Rotation
cues: Sit in the 90/90 shape and hinge forward over the front shin.
Chest stays tall as it comes down -- do not round to get lower.
Stop where the outside of the front hip pulls, and breathe there.

exercises.name: Lying 90/90 Hip Shift
cues: On your back, feet on a wall or box with hips and knees at right angles.
Breathe all the way out and feel the low back settle onto the floor.
Shift the weight gently side to side without lifting the hips.

exercises.name: Lateral Kneeling Adductor Rock
cues: Kneel on one knee with the other leg straight out to the side.
Rock the hips back and across towards the kneeling side.
Keep the straight leg's foot flat and the toes pointing forward.

exercises.name: Lateral Kneeling Adductor PNF
cues: Take the same kneeling side-split position out to a light stretch.
Pull the straight leg's heel into the floor for five seconds.
Relax, rock a little further, and repeat it three times.

exercises.name: Half-Kneeling Short Adductor Mobilization
cues: Kneel side-on with the outside leg bent and the knee out on the floor.
Rock towards that bent knee to reach the groin muscles nearer the hip.
Bent knee means short adductors -- straight leg is a different muscle.

exercises.name: Straight-Leg Adductor Squeeze
cues: On your back with the legs long and something soft between the ankles.
Squeeze the ankles together and hold, breathing normally.
Groin muscles work here, not the glutes -- keep the backside relaxed.

exercises.name: Side-Lying Adductor Pullback
cues: Lie on one side with the top leg forward and resting on a box.
Draw the bottom leg back and lift it a little, toes pointing down.
Small and slow -- the range here is a few inches, not a foot.

exercises.name: Lying Glute Stretch
cues: On your back, pull one knee across the body towards the far shoulder.
Keep both shoulders flat on the floor as the knee travels.
Stop where the back pocket pulls, not where the low back lifts.

exercises.name: Posterior Hip Rock
cues: On hands and knees, rock the hips back towards the heels.
Stop the moment the low back starts to round underneath you.
That stopping point is the range you have; rock in and out of it.

exercises.name: Leg Cradle
cues: Walking forward, pick up one shin and hug it into the chest.
Hold the knee and the ankle, and stand up tall on the other leg.
One per step, alternating sides as you travel.

exercises.name: Half-Kneeling Arm Arc
cues: Half-kneeling side-on, the outside hand tracing the floor by your hip.
Sweep that arm in a big slow arc overhead and back down behind you.
Keep the ribs down; let the arm go further than the back does.

exercises.name: Wide-Knee Arm Arc
cues: Kneel with the knees wide and sit the hips back towards the heels.
Sweep one arm in a long arc across the floor and up overhead.
The wide knees hold the hips still so only the upper back turns.

exercises.name: Side-Lying Arm Arc
cues: Lie on your side, knees bent up, both arms stacked out in front.
Trace the top hand in a wide arc over your head and round behind.
Follow the hand with your eyes and let the chest open as it goes.

exercises.name: Mini-Band Elvis
cues: Band above the knees, feet planted a bit wider than the hips.
Drive one knee out and let the other roll in, then swap. Quick and light.
The feet do not move at all -- everything happens at the hips.

exercises.name: Three-Way Adductor Squeeze
cues: On your back with something soft between the knees, feet up close.
Squeeze and hold, then repeat with the feet further out, then legs long.
Three hip angles, and the groin should do the work at all three.

exercises.name: Rotational Squat
cues: From standing, pivot a quarter turn and sink into that hip.
Both feet turn with you -- do not leave one behind and twist the knee.
Come back up the way you went down, then go the other way.

exercises.name: Quadruped Breathing
cues: On hands and knees with the back flat and the head in line.
Breathe out slowly and fully, letting the ribs drop towards the floor.
Pause at empty for a count before you let the next breath in.

exercises.name: Quadruped Pelvic Tilt Hold
cues: On hands and knees, tuck the tailbone under and flatten the low back.
Hold that shape and keep breathing -- do not hold your breath instead.
The movement is small; the ribs and shoulders stay where they are.

exercises.name: Quadruped Hip Extension
cues: On hands and knees, press one leg straight back and slightly up.
Squeeze that glute to lift it, and stop before the low back arches.
The hips stay level and square to the floor throughout.

exercises.name: Quadruped Bent-Knee Hip Extension
cues: On hands and knees, keep one knee bent and press that foot to the ceiling.
Drive from the glute; the low back must not take over the lift.
A bent knee keeps the hamstring out of it, which is the point.

exercises.name: Quadruped Adductor Squeeze
cues: On hands and knees with something soft squeezed between the knees.
Press the knees together and hold, keeping the back flat.
Breathe out through the squeeze rather than bracing against it.

exercises.name: Quadruped Thoracic Rotation
cues: On hands and knees, one hand behind the head, elbow tucked down.
Turn that elbow up to the ceiling and follow it with your eyes.
Hips stay square -- if they turn too, the low back is doing it.

exercises.name: Lateral Kneeling Thoracic Rotation
cues: Kneel side-on with the outside leg out and that foot flat.
Hands behind the head, then turn the chest open towards the ceiling.
Turn from the ribs; the hips stay set where the legs put them.

exercises.name: Half-Kneeling Thoracic Rotation with Side Bend
cues: Half-kneeling, hands behind the head, ribs stacked over the hips.
Turn towards the front leg, then add a lean away over the back hip.
Squeeze the back glute the whole time so the low back stays out of it.

exercises.name: Side-Lying Thoracic Rotation
cues: On your side, knees bent up and stacked, arms together in front.
Open the top arm across and back, reaching for the floor behind you.
Keep the knees pinned together so the turn comes from the ribs.

exercises.name: Rock-Back Thoracic Rotation
cues: On hands and knees, sit the hips back towards the heels first.
From there, reach one arm under the body, then open it to the ceiling.
Sitting back locks the low back so the upper back has to do the turning.

exercises.name: Bench Thoracic Mobilization
cues: Kneel in front of a bench and rest both elbows on it, hands together.
Sit the hips back and let the chest sink down between the arms.
Breathe out at the bottom and let it settle a little further.

exercises.name: Standing Thoracic Rotation, Foot on Box
cues: One foot up on a box, hands behind the head, standing tall.
Turn the chest towards the raised knee and hold a beat at the end.
The raised leg pins the hip so the rotation stays in the ribs.

exercises.name: Wide-Knee Reach Under
cues: Kneel with the knees wide, hips back, one hand planted in front.
Thread the other arm under the body as far across as it will go.
Let that shoulder come to the floor and turn the head to follow.

exercises.name: Standing Pec Mobilization
cues: Forearm flat on a doorway or upright, elbow at about shoulder height.
Turn the chest away from that arm until the front of the shoulder pulls.
Try it again with the elbow higher and lower to catch the whole muscle.

exercises.name: Cross-Body Lat Mobilization
cues: Hold an upright with one hand high and sit the hips back and away.
Push the hips across to the opposite side from the holding arm.
You want the pull down the side of the ribs, not in the shoulder joint.

exercises.name: Spiderman
cues: From a push-up position, step one foot up outside the same hand.
Sink the hips towards the floor and keep the back leg long.
Hold a beat at the bottom, then step it back and swap sides.

exercises.name: Alternating Spiderman
cues: Step one foot outside the hand, then straight back and swap.
Keep it moving -- no hold at the bottom on this version.
Hips stay low the whole time instead of bobbing up between reps.

exercises.name: Spiderman with Arm Arc
cues: Step into the spiderman and plant the inside hand on the floor.
Sweep the free arm in a wide arc from the floor to overhead and back.
Follow the hand with your eyes and let the chest turn with it.

exercises.name: Spiderman to Hamstring
cues: Step into the spiderman, then push the hips back and straighten the front leg.
Toes of the front foot come up as the leg goes long.
Rock between the two ends slowly instead of holding either one.

exercises.name: Downward Dog
cues: Hands and feet down, hips pushed high into an upside-down V.
Push the floor away and let the head drop between the arms.
Bend one knee then the other to work each calf in turn.

exercises.name: Lying Floor Slides
cues: On your back, knees bent, arms out in a goalpost on the floor.
Slide both arms overhead keeping the wrists and elbows down.
Low back stays flat -- if the ribs flare, you have gone past your range.

exercises.name: Lying Alternating Floor Slides
cues: Same shape on your back, but slide one arm up as the other comes down.
Both arms stay in contact with the floor the whole way.
Slow and even; the ribs must not lift as the arms pass each other.

exercises.name: Hip Lift March
cues: Bridge the hips up and hold them there, ribs down.
Lift one knee towards the chest without letting that hip drop.
Put it down softly and take the other one. The hips never sag.

exercises.name: Single-Leg Hip Lift
cues: One foot down, the other knee hugged towards the chest.
Push through that heel and lift the hips until the body is one line.
Both hips rise together -- do not let the free side drop back.

exercises.name: Hip Lift with Adductor Squeeze
cues: On your back with something soft squeezed between the knees.
Squeeze the knees in first, then push the hips up and hold.
Breathe out at the top; the groin and glutes work together here.

exercises.name: Double Leg Lower
cues: On your back, legs straight up, low back pressed into the floor.
Lower both legs only as far as the back stays flat, then bring them up.
The moment the back lifts you have found your range. Go no further.

exercises.name: Band-Supported Leg Lower
cues: On your back, a band round one foot with that leg held up.
Lower the other leg towards the floor while the band holds its side.
Only go as low as the low back can stay flat on the floor.

exercises.name: Bear Position Pelvic Tilt
cues: Hands and knees, then lift the knees a couple of inches off the floor.
Hold there and tuck the tailbone under to flatten the low back.
Keep breathing -- this gets held with the breath by mistake.

exercises.name: Box Quad Mobilization
cues: Half-kneeling with the back shin up against a box behind you.
Squeeze the back glute and tuck the tailbone before you lean in.
The stretch belongs in the front of the thigh and hip, not the knee.

exercises.name: Box Quad with Reach Over
cues: Set up in the box quad position with the glute already squeezed.
Reach the same-side arm up and lean away over the front leg.
That reach takes the stretch up the front of the hip into the ribs.

exercises.name: Box Hip Flexor Mobilization
cues: Back foot up on a low box, front foot forward and flat.
Tuck the tailbone and drive the back hip forward, ribs down.
Do not lean back to feel it more; that just arches the low back.

exercises.name: Box Hip Rotator Mobilization
cues: Shin across the top of a box, front knee bent to a right angle.
Keep the chest tall and hinge forward over that front shin.
Stop where the outside of the hip pulls, and back off if the knee talks.

exercises.name: Box Hip Rotator with Thoracic Rotation
cues: Set the shin across the box, then place both hands behind the head.
Turn the chest open away from the front leg and hold a beat.
The hip stays where the box put it; only the ribs turn.

exercises.name: Half-Kneeling Quad Mobilization
cues: Half-kneeling with the back shin up the wall behind you.
Squeeze that glute and tuck the tailbone before you sit tall.
Come out of it if the kneecap complains rather than the thigh.

exercises.name: Half-Kneeling Quad PNF
cues: Take the wall quad position out to a light stretch, glute squeezed.
Press the back shin into the wall for five seconds, then let go.
Sit a little taller each time. Three rounds is plenty.

exercises.name: Half-Kneeling Overhead Reach
cues: Half-kneeling, back glute squeezed, ribs stacked over the hips.
Reach the back-leg-side arm straight overhead and slightly across.
If the ribs flare to get the arm up, lower the arm instead.

exercises.name: Half-Kneeling Band Pull-Apart
cues: Half-kneeling with a band held at shoulder height, arms long.
Pull the band apart until the arms are wide, squeezing the shoulder blades.
The kneeling stance is there to stop you leaning back into it.

exercises.name: Brettzel
cues: On your side, top knee bent up and held down by the bottom hand.
Reach back and catch the bottom foot with the free hand.
Now turn the chest towards the ceiling and breathe. Go slowly here.

exercises.name: Supported Hip Airplane
cues: Hold an upright and stand on one leg, hinged forward at the hip.
Rotate the free hip open to the ceiling, then closed towards the floor.
The standing foot stays planted; the turn happens at that hip.

exercises.name: Lying Knee to Knee
cues: On your back, feet wide and flat, knees bent up.
Let both knees drop to one side, then across to the other.
Shoulders stay down; this is the hips rotating, not the spine.

exercises.name: Wide-Knee Hip Internal Rotation
cues: Kneel with the knees wide and the hips sat back towards the heels.
Let one hip roll inward so that thigh turns in, then the other.
Small range and slow. Internal rotation is usually the stiff one.

exercises.name: Tall-Kneeling Hip Rotation
cues: Tall on both knees, one foot lifted off the floor behind you.
Swing that lower leg out to the side, then across behind the other.
The hips stay square and facing forward the whole time.

exercises.name: Side-Lying Shoulder Circle
cues: On your side, knees bent, top arm resting along the body.
Draw the biggest slow circle you can with that hand, going backwards.
Let the shoulder blade travel with the arm rather than holding it still.

exercises.name: Quadruped Forearm Mobilization
cues: On hands and knees with the palms down and fingers turned back.
Rock the hips gently backwards until the forearms pull, then return.
Turn the hands out and in to reach different parts of the forearm.

exercises.name: Mini-Band Reaching Squat
cues: Band above the knees, feet about shoulder width apart.
Squat down and reach both arms forward as a counterweight.
Push the knees out against the band the whole way down and up.

exercises.name: Mini-Band Step-Out
cues: Band round the ankles, knees soft, standing on one leg.
Step the other foot out to the side against the band and back.
The standing hip does the work of holding you level. Do not lean.

exercises.name: Three-Way Lunge
cues: Lunge straight forward, back to the middle, then out to the side.
Third one goes back and across behind you, like a curtsy.
Same leg does all three before you swap over.

exercises.name: Lateral Lunge with Rotation
cues: Step out wide and sit into that hip, the other leg staying long.
From the bottom, turn the chest open over the bent leg.
Come back square before you push out of it.

exercises.name: Reverse Lunge with Rotation
cues: Step back into a lunge and drop the back knee towards the floor.
Turn the chest over the front thigh, arms reaching wide.
Turn back to square, then stand up out of the lunge.

exercises.name: Reverse Lunge to Hamstring Stretch
cues: Step back into a lunge and sink the hips down.
Then push the hips back and straighten the front leg, toes up.
One rep is both halves. Alternate legs as you travel forward.

exercises.name: Knee to Chest into Overhead Lunge
cues: Walking forward, pull one knee to the chest and stand tall.
Put that foot down into a lunge and reach both arms overhead.
Ribs stay down as the arms go up, then walk on to the other side.

exercises.name: Reaching Quad Stretch
cues: Standing, catch one ankle behind you and squeeze that glute.
Reach the opposite arm up and over, leaning away from the held leg.
Balance on the standing leg rather than grabbing something.

exercises.name: Skate-Position Hip Circles
cues: Stand on one leg in a quarter squat, the other foot on a slider.
Draw slow circles out to the side with the sliding foot.
The standing hip holds you level; that is the work, not the circle.

exercises.name: Lateral Squat
cues: Feet planted wide and pointing forward, and they stay there.
Shift across and sit into one hip, letting the other leg go straight.
Both feet stay flat -- no stepping in and out between reps.

exercises.name: Bear Position Shoulder Taps
cues: Hands and knees, knees hovering just off the floor.
Take one hand off and tap the opposite shoulder, then swap.
The hips must not rock -- that stillness is the whole exercise.

exercises.name: Band-Assisted Plyo Push-Up
cues: Band slung under the chest from an upright on each side.
Push hard enough to leave the floor; the band buys you the height.
Land on soft elbows and reset the shape before the next rep.

exercises.name: Neutral-Grip Inverted Row
cues: Palms facing each other on a pair of handles rather than a straight bar.
Pull the chest between the hands, elbows brushing the ribs.
The neutral grip is kinder on the elbows if a straight bar nags.

exercises.name: Mini-Band Forward Walk
cues: Band round the ankles, knees soft, hips sat back a little.
Walk forward taking each step out and forward on a diagonal.
Never let the band go slack, and keep the steps short.

exercises.name: Diagonal Hip PNF
cues: On your back, take one leg up and across the body to a light stretch.
Push that leg back against your own hand for five seconds, then relax.
Take up the new range and repeat. Three rounds each side.

exercises.name: Side-Lying Glute Breathing
cues: On your side, knees bent up in front, top knee resting on the floor.
Squeeze the top glute gently and hold it while you breathe out fully.
Long slow breaths -- this is a settling drill, not a stretch.

exercises.name: Cross-Reaching Lat Stretch
cues: Kneel with the hips back and both hands out in front of you.
Walk one hand across to the far side and let that side of the ribs open.
Then thread it underneath and turn the chest towards the floor.

exercises.name: Lateral Kneeling Foot Rotation
cues: Kneel side-on with the outside leg out and that foot flat.
Roll that foot slowly onto its inside edge, then its outside edge.
The knee follows the foot; keep the heel down for both.

exercises.name: Cat-Cow
cues: On all fours, hands under the shoulders and knees under the hips.
Round the spine one segment at a time, then reverse into extension.
Move with the breath and stop short of any pinch in the low back.

exercises.name: Thread the Needle
cues: From all fours, slide one arm under the body, palm facing up.
Let that shoulder rest down while the hips stay stacked over the knees.
Return by reaching the same arm to the ceiling, then alternate.

exercises.name: Banded Shoulder Dislocate
cues: Hold a light band wide, arms straight, thumbs up.
Sweep the band overhead and behind you, keeping the elbows locked.
Widen the grip until it passes without shrugging or arching the back.

exercises.name: Scapular Wall Slide
cues: Stand with the back, arms and hands flat against the wall.
Slide the arms overhead without letting the ribs or wrists leave the wall.
Stop where contact breaks; that range is the rep.

exercises.name: Shoulder CARs
cues: Stand tall, one arm straight, and trace the largest circle you can.
Keep the ribs down and the opposite shoulder still.
Slow and deliberate; a single circle should take several seconds.

exercises.name: Hip CARs
cues: Stand tall, hold something for balance, lift one knee to hip height.
Trace the biggest circle you can with that knee, out and around.
Keep the pelvis square; only the hip moves.

exercises.name: Ankle Dorsiflexion Rock
cues: Half-kneeling, front foot flat, heel glued to the floor.
Drive the knee forward over the toes, then rock back out.
The moment the heel lifts you have gone past the range.

exercises.name: Adductor Rock-Back
cues: On all fours, extend one leg out to the side with the foot flat.
Rock the hips back toward the heels, then return.
Keep the low back flat; the stretch belongs in the inner thigh.

exercises.name: Deep Squat Hold
cues: Feet shoulder-width, toes slightly out, sink as low as you can.
Elbows inside the knees, pushing them gently out.
Chest up and heels down; hold a doorframe if you need balance.

exercises.name: Child's Pose
cues: Kneel, big toes together, knees wide, sit back onto the heels.
Reach the arms long and let the chest sink toward the floor.
Breathe into the back of the ribs and let the shoulders relax.

exercises.name: Dead Hang
cues: Hang from a bar, hands shoulder-width, grip firm.
Let the shoulders travel up toward the ears and stay relaxed.
Keep the ribs down, and step off before the grip fails.

exercises.name: Leg Swing
cues: Hold a wall for balance and stand tall.
Swing one leg front to back, then side to side, staying relaxed.
Let the range build over reps rather than forcing the first swing.

exercises.name: Standing Calf Stretch
cues: Hands on a wall, one foot back, back leg straight.
Press the back heel into the floor and lean in from the ankle.
Keep the back foot pointing forward, not turned out.

exercises.name: Seated Hamstring Stretch
cues: Sit tall, one leg straight, the other foot tucked to the inner thigh.
Hinge forward from the hips rather than rounding the back.
Stop at a strong stretch behind the thigh, breathe out, and hold.

exercises.name: Standing Quad Stretch
cues: Stand tall, steady yourself on a wall, pull one heel to the glute.
Keep the knees side by side and the tailbone tucked under.
Ease the hip forward; do not arch the lower back to get more.

exercises.name: Supine Figure-Four Stretch
cues: Lie on your back, one ankle crossed over the opposite thigh.
Reach through and draw the bottom thigh toward your chest.
Keep the head and shoulders down; it should bite deep in the glute.

exercises.name: Seated Spinal Twist
cues: Sit tall, one knee crossed over the opposite leg, that foot flat.
Rotate toward the top knee, the elbow acting as a gentle lever.
Turn from the mid-back and keep both sit bones on the floor.

exercises.name: Prone Press-Up
cues: Lie face down, hands under the shoulders, hips staying on the floor.
Press the chest up only as far as stays comfortable.
Let the lower back relax into it, and back off if anything pinches.

exercises.name: Cross-Body Shoulder Stretch
cues: Bring one arm straight across the chest at shoulder height.
Draw it in with the other forearm, just above the elbow.
Keep the shoulder down rather than shrugged toward the ear.

exercises.name: Overhead Triceps Stretch
cues: Reach one hand down your spine, elbow pointing at the ceiling.
Use the other hand to draw that elbow gently back and in.
Keep the ribs down instead of arching the lower back.

exercises.name: Soleus Stretch
cues: Set up like a calf stretch, then bend the back knee toward the wall.
Keep that heel flat on the floor the whole time.
It should sit low near the Achilles, not up in the calf belly.

exercises.name: Kneeling Ankle Stretch
cues: Kneel with the toes tucked under and sit back onto the heels.
Share the weight evenly, and come up if the toes cramp.
Hands on the floor in front take weight off if it is too strong.

exercises.name: Wall Lat Stretch
cues: Hands on a wall at hip height, feet walked back, arms straight.
Sink the chest toward the floor with the hips over the heels.
Feel it along the side of the ribs and under the armpits.

exercises.name: Butterfly Stretch
cues: Sit with the soles of the feet together and the heels drawn in.
Sit tall first, then hinge forward from the hips.
Let the knees fall open on their own; never push them down.

exercises.name: Upper Trap Stretch
cues: Sit tall, one hand under the opposite thigh to anchor that shoulder.
Tilt the ear toward the other shoulder until it is a mild stretch.
No rotation and no hard pulling; the neck takes a gentle dose only.

exercises.name: Glute Bridge
cues: Lie on your back, knees bent, feet flat and close to the hips.
Push through the heels until hips, knees and shoulders line up.
Squeeze the glutes at the top; do not arch the low back to get higher.

exercises.name: Knee CARs
cues: Seated or standing on one leg, hold the thigh still with both hands.
Trace the largest slow circle you can with the heel.
Only the knee moves; if the hip joins in, shrink the circle.

exercises.name: Ankle CARs
cues: Seated, lift one foot clear of the floor and hold the shin still.
Trace the biggest circle you can with the toes, both directions.
Keep the knee quiet; the movement is all ankle.

exercises.name: Squat to Stand
cues: Feet shoulder width, reach down and hold on under the toes.
Pull yourself into a deep squat and lift the chest tall.
Keep the grip and straighten the legs to stand; repeat smoothly.

exercises.name: Walking Quad Pull
cues: Walking forward, catch one ankle behind you and pull the heel to the hip.
Stand tall and squeeze the glute on that side.
Hold for a step, release into the next stride, then alternate.

exercises.name: Inchworm
cues: From standing, hinge over and walk the hands out to a straight plank.
Keep the hips level and the ribs down as you walk out.
Walk the feet back to the hands, legs as long as is comfortable.

exercises.name: Scorpion
cues: Lie face down with the arms out wide and the palms flat.
Reach one heel across and behind toward the opposite hand.
Keep both shoulders down; rotate only as far as they stay on the floor.

exercises.name: Bodyweight Hip Hinge
cues: Feet hip width, hands on the belly and low back to feel the position.
Push the hips back and let the chest fall, keeping the back flat.
Go only as low as the back stays flat, then drive the hips forward.

exercises.name: Half-Kneeling Inline Cable Lift
cues: Half-kneeling with the back toes and front heel on one line, as if on a rail.
Pulley low, handle outside the down knee, lifting up across to the far shoulder.
The narrow base is the point -- if you topple, widen it until you can hold still.
Turn the ribs, not the arms, and keep the down-side glute switched on.

exercises.name: Half-Kneeling Inline Cable Chop
cues: Half-kneeling, back toes and front heel stacked on a single line.
Pulley high, handle above the far shoulder, chopping down past the down knee.
The ribs do the work; the arms only carry the handle where the ribs send it.
Come back up under control -- the cable should never pull you off the line.

exercises.name: Resisted Bear Crawl
cues: Belt or band around the hips, anchored behind you, crawling out against it.
Hands and toes only, knees hovering an inch off the floor the whole way.
Opposite hand and foot move together, in short steps against the pull.
Hips stay low and level; the band will try to twist them, do not let it.

exercises.name: Turkish Get-Up
cues: The whole sequence: elbow, hand, hip lift, sweep the leg through, stand up.
The bell arm stays locked and vertical from the floor to standing and back.
Eyes stay on the bell until you are upright, then look straight ahead.
Reverse it step by step. Getting back down is where reps are usually lost.

exercises.name: Half-Kneeling Dumbbell Row
cues: Half-kneeling, bell in the hand on the same side as the back knee.
Hinge over the front thigh with a flat back and let the arm hang long.
Pull to the hip with the elbow close, then let the shoulder blade travel out.
The down knee is what stops you rowing with the whole body.

exercises.name: Half-Kneeling Bottoms-Up Press
cues: Half-kneeling, bell held upside down with the handle squeezed hard.
Pressing arm on the same side as the down knee; ribs down, glute tight.
Press slowly straight up past the ear -- speed is what tips the bell over.
Go far lighter than a normal press. The grip is the limit, not the shoulder.

exercises.name: Sandbag Squat
cues: Bag hugged high across the chest, elbows underneath it and forearms tight.
Sit straight down; the load pulls you forward, so the chest has to fight up.
Stand all the way tall before the next rep -- the bag shifts if you rush.

exercises.name: Offset Squat
cues: One bell only, held at one shoulder. The feet still stay square.
Squat straight down and refuse to lean towards the loaded side.
The work is the anti-lean, not the weight -- light is enough here.
Do the same reps again with the bell on the other shoulder.

exercises.name: Goblet Split Squat
cues: Bell against the chest, feet set in a lunge and left there for the set.
Drop straight down until the back knee is just off the floor.
Push through the front heel; the bell keeps the chest upright for you.

exercises.name: Goblet Lateral Squat
cues: Bell at the chest, feet planted wide and pointing forward throughout.
Shift across and sit into one hip while the other leg goes straight.
Both feet stay flat -- no stepping in and out between reps.
The bell counterweights you, so you can sit lower than empty-handed.

exercises.name: Goblet Slideboard Lateral Squat
cues: Bell at the chest, one foot on the board, the other planted on the floor.
Slide the board foot out sideways and sit into the planted hip.
Pull it back in with the inner thigh -- that is the half people skip.
Slide only as far as you can stand back up from without a wobble.

exercises.name: Goblet Walking Lunge
cues: Bell held against the chest, elbows tucked under it, ribs down.
Step out and drop the back knee towards the floor, not forwards.
Push through the front heel to bring the back foot through.
The front-loaded bell pulls you forward; stay tall against it.

exercises.name: Double Kettlebell Walking Lunge
cues: A bell hanging in each hand, arms long, shoulders pulled down and back.
Step out and drop the back knee, letting the bells hang either side.
Grip usually gives out before the legs do -- a fair place to stop.

exercises.name: Double Kettlebell Rack Walking Lunge
cues: Both bells in the front rack, wrists straight, elbows tight to the ribs.
Breathe shallow and keep the ribs down; the rack tries to push them up.
Step out and drop the back knee with the torso dead vertical.
The rack is the hard part. Drop to one bell before the chest folds.

exercises.name: Front-Rack Reverse Lunge
cues: Bells in the front rack, elbows down, ribs tucked before the first step.
Step backwards and drop that knee to the floor, torso staying vertical.
Push through the front heel to bring the back foot home.
Stepping back is kinder to the knee than stepping forward under load.

exercises.name: Double Kettlebell Deadlift
cues: A bell outside each foot, hips back, chest up, arms long.
Push the floor away and stand tall, squeezing the glutes at the top.
Two bells load the hinge heavier without needing a bar or a rack.

exercises.name: Slide Single-Leg Romanian Deadlift
cues: A bell in each hand, the free foot resting on a slider behind you.
Hinge over the standing leg and let the slider travel straight back.
The slider takes the balance out of it, so the hamstring gets the work.
Hips stay square -- do not let the sliding side roll open.

exercises.name: Feet-Elevated Hip Lift
cues: Shoulders on the floor, both heels up on a bench, knees bent.
Drive through the heels until the hips are level with the knees.
Squeeze the glutes at the top; do not arch the low back to get higher.

exercises.name: Medial-Lateral Box Hop
cues: Stand beside a low box and hop sideways onto it with both feet.
Hop down the far side and go straight into the next one.
Land soft and quiet, knees tracking over the toes and never caving in.
Keep the box low -- height is not what this drill is training.

exercises.name: Lateral Hurdle Hop
cues: Hurdles in a line beside you, hopping sideways over each, feet together.
Stay stiff through the ankles and spend as little time down as you can.
Knees stay pointing forward; the hips carry you across, not a twist.
End the set when the heels start touching down between hurdles.

exercises.name: Shuttle Jump
cues: Pick a line and jump forward over it with both feet, then straight back.
Small and fast -- the aim is quick ground contacts, not distance.
Stay on the balls of the feet with the knees soft the whole set.

exercises.name: Lean-Fall Run
cues: Stand tall, whole body straight, and lean forward from the ankles.
Keep leaning until you have to run, then run out of the fall.
Do not bend at the waist -- ankle to head stays one straight line.
The first steps should feel like catching yourself. That is acceleration.

exercises.name: Band-Resisted Lateral Shuffle
cues: Band round the hips, anchored to one side so it pulls you back.
Half-squat stance, shuffling away from the anchor, feet never crossing.
Drive the ground away with the trail leg on every step.
Come back the other way so both legs get the resisted direction.

exercises.name: Sled Crossover
cues: Side-on to the sled with the strap held at the hips, sled behind you.
Travel sideways, crossing the trail leg over in front then behind.
Open the hip towards where you are going as the leg crosses.
Come back the other way so both hips do the crossing.

exercises.name: Sideways Sled Push
cues: Side-on to the sled, both hands on the upright, arms locked out.
Drive it along with short lateral steps, hips low and shoulders square.
Push with the legs; the arms are only there to hold the line.
Same distance back facing the other way.

exercises.name: Ladder Quick Through
cues: Two feet into each rung, one-two, then two feet into the next.
Stay on the balls of the feet and keep the contacts light and fast.
Hips stay square down the ladder; the feet work, not the shoulders.
Rhythm beats speed. Ragged and fast teaches nothing.

exercises.name: Ladder Quick Stick
cues: One-two through a rung, then land on one leg outside it and freeze.
Stick it dead still for a beat before the next -- no hop, no stumble.
Land soft with the knee over the toes and the hip taking the force.
Alternate which leg sticks as you work down the ladder.
